$schema: https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema $id: urn:job-application:contracts:evidence-kernel:0.1.0 title: Shared evidence kernel description: >- Review draft for recording discovery, practice, and production work without turning declarations, transport acknowledgements, or missing observations into success. This schema defines six durable record types. All references to schema definitions are local to this file. x-status: proposed x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt, Parts VI and VIII: versioned shared evidence contract."
x-source-index: handoff: &h "1-handoff-brief.txt, Parts VI and VIII–X" boundary: &b "1-handoff-brief.txt, Parts III–V" storage: &s "2-state-bank-crawler-blueprint.json, §11 and Decision 8" lease: &l "2-state-bank-crawler-blueprint.json, §11.15" diagnostic: &d "3-hellscape-blueprint.md, §§4 and 10" fixture: &f "3-hellscape-blueprint.md, §§6.5, 9, 10, and 12" qualification: &q "5-browser-qualification.md, Evidence discipline" native: &n "4-circus-tent-arch.md, §§5.6–5.8" product: &j "6-get-a-job.xml.txt, capability_profile.txt and job_search_queries.txt" wire: &w >- Proposed wire design implementing 1-handoff-brief.txt Parts VI and VIII; identifiers, discriminators, encodings, and local type names are contract proposals, not claims about existing implementations.
x-contract: name: evidence-kernel version: 0.1.0 maturity: review_draft owner: contracts consumers: [crawler, Circus Tent, Ringmaster, Hellscape, job-hunter] conformance_suite: conformance/00-evidence-kernel.md validation_gate: structural_validation_and_semantic_rules reference_implementation: product: Hellscape milestone: M1 implementation_status: planned_not_certified x-status: extracted x-source: *h purpose: >- Permit a real manually executed application to be commissioned, evidenced, and tracked before any browser executor or laboratory is available. Laboratory results improve execution; they do not replace production work. x-status: inferred x-source: "Governing task; 1-handoff-brief.txt Parts VII–X; 6-get-a-job.xml.txt capability_profile.txt."
x-ownership: x-status: inferred x-source: *h records: manifest: >- The run commissioner authors the input; the admitting kernel authenticates and freezes it. Later changes require a new manifest, not an in-place edit. journal_event: >- Exactly one journal authority assigns ordering, ingestion provenance, event identities, and hashes. Producers author only their authorized content. Journal authority is not authority over every business fact. diagnostic: >- The diagnostic analyzer writes immutable derived revisions. It may assess claims against facts but may not overwrite either. replay_receipt: >- The replay worker writes an immutable receipt about an offline replay. It has no authority to repeat a production action. lease_record: >- The resource owner's lease authority writes the lease domain and its journal atomically. Workers request changes; they do not self-issue leases. capability_descriptor: >- The authenticated subject connector or native binding declares a scoped descriptor. Consumers assess evidence independently. Declaration is not self-certification.
x-validation: x-status: proposed x-source: *w requirements: - >- Decode YAML into JSON-compatible values before validation. Reject duplicate mapping keys, non-finite numbers, and values outside declared numeric bounds. YAML anchors in this schema are annotation abbreviations, not wire features. - >- Enforce JSON Schema 2020-12, including date-time format assertions. Reject unknown record versions and unknown properties on closed objects. Never insert success, zero, false, or an empty object as a missing-value default. - >- A JSON Schema pass establishes structural validity only. Full conformance also requires every applicable EK rule below: authorization, hash checking, reference resolution, cross-field arithmetic, and transition fencing. - >- The only accepted serialized null is Missing.value. Raw native bytes may contain literal nulls, but must remain in an artifact until explicitly normalized. Omitting a required field is not an alternative to Missing. - >- Event-specific business data uses EvidenceMap. Its interpretation is owned by the registered event kind and version, not by a generic success heuristic. Observed numeric metrics and durations belong in Measurement, not hidden untyped timing fields in data.
x-canonicalization: profile: kernel-jcs-sha256/1 x-status: proposed x-source: *w rationale: >- One specified byte representation is needed for independent Go, Rust, Python, and TypeScript implementations to agree on evidence identities. rules: encoding: UTF-8 structured_bytes: RFC8785_JSON_Canonicalization_Scheme digest: "sha256:<64 lowercase hexadecimal digits>" artifact_digest: SHA-256_of_exact_stored_bytes manifest_digest: SHA-256_of_canonical_complete_manifest event_digest: SHA-256_of_canonical_event_with_only_event_hash_removed diagnostic_digest: SHA-256_of_canonical_complete_diagnostic journal_prefix_digest: event_hash_at_last_sequence ordering: Preserve_array_order_and_string_contents exclusions: >- Do not silently redact, normalize Unicode, reorder arrays, or omit null envelopes while hashing. A redacted export is a different artifact with a journaled derivation, not the original bytes under the original digest. flip_condition: >- Change the profile only through a versioned contract revision if cross-language conformance exposes an ambiguity or an unsupported numeric representation. Existing receipts continue to name their original profile.
x-source-reconciliation: - decision: >- The handoff's capability, opportunity, and result enums are authoritative. Hellscape's extra blocked and not_applicable result values are not retained. A legacy blocked result becomes opportunity=blocked plus not_exercised or indeterminate according to the evidence. Inapplicability is recorded in capability/scope and rationale, with result=not_exercised. x-status: extracted x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part VI overrides 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §4.4." - decision: >- Hellscape's nullable fields become typed Missing envelopes with exactly the handoff's six reasons. manual_fixture_validation is a rationale, not a seventh null reason. x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part VI; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§4.2–4.5." - decision: >- Hellscape's flat timing fields become a discriminated estimate. A native zero remains an exact subject-reported zero; it is neither discarded nor substituted for an unavailable independently measured interval. x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part VI; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§1.3, 4.5, 10.4." - decision: >- Stage1's authoritative lease time is retained, but A5's assumed clock skew and its default lease duration are not portfolio guarantees. Lease comparisons use one authority clock epoch; restart fencing is explicit. x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part VI; 2-state-bank-crawler-blueprint.json A5 and §11.15." - decision: >- A native completed response remains an execution claim unless its documented semantics establish something narrower or stronger. Firestore tracker status and a native response status cannot become a portfolio-wide outcome. x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part VI; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §4.6; 6-get-a-job.xml.txt docs/contracts/firestore-collections.md." - decision: >- Replay receipts are separate immutable records. Publishing a replay result does not mutate the diagnostic it compared or introduce a self-referential diagnostic hash. x-status: proposed x-source: *d - decision: >- Qualification's evidence discipline is retained. Its standalone product, exit-code gate, and particular live-workflow restrictions do not become prerequisites for commissioning a job application. x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Parts I, V, VII–IX; 5-browser-qualification.md." - decision: >- No governing handoff invariant or provisional is amended by this file. Wire-format proposals below make the handoff implementable without certifying any current native deployment. x-status: proposed x-source: *w
x-semantic-rules: - id: EK-JOURNAL classification: invariant rule: >- An acknowledged event is durably appended. Sequences are contiguous and strictly increasing within a journal, beginning at 1. The first event is manifest_admitted and pins the complete immutable manifest. All subsequent events name the same run, journal, and manifest digest. Events are never edited, deleted, resequenced, or backdated into an earlier prefix. consequence: >- A diagnostic may cite only events in its named prefix, including locally journaled imports. Materialized state, logs, screenshots, and memory not registered in that prefix are not independent evidence for that diagnostic. derivation: >- Retroactively adding evidence would make a previously published diagnostic impossible to reproduce. x-status: extracted x-source: *h
- id: EK-ATOMICITY classification: invariant rule: >- A locally authoritative operation commits its admitted input, idempotency record, authoritative effects, journal events, and replayable response as one owner-local durable effect before acknowledgement. Install referenced artifact bytes durably before that commit. Cross-owner publication remains asynchronous; this rule does not authorize a shared transaction across owners. consequence: >- A remote employer's action cannot be atomically committed with this journal. Persist intent before dispatch and retain uncertain delivery or outcome when acknowledgement evidence is missing. Never replay the external write merely to repair the local journal. derivation: >- Separate log and effect commits can claim an effect that did not occur or lose evidence of an effect that did. x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part VI; 2-state-bank-crawler-blueprint.json Decision 8; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§10.1, 10.6."
- id: EK-HASHES classification: proposed_mechanism rule: >- Verify all content digests. At sequence 1, previous_event_hash is Missing(not_applicable). At sequence n>1 it equals event_hash at n-1. JournalPrefix.head_hash equals the event hash at last_sequence. Resolve an EvidenceRef by journal, sequence, event ID, hash, and JSON pointer; all must agree. A hash chain detects changed content but is not authentication. x-status: proposed x-source: *w
- id: EK-PROVENANCE classification: invariant rule: >- The ingestion authority assigns producer identity, provenance, owner_domain, role, assertion_kind, event ID, sequence, receipt time, and hashes using authenticated producer registration and the manifest's event registry. Untrusted callers submit EventSubmission, never JournalEnvelope. Reject submitted server/provenance/authority fields rather than trusting them. consequence: >- Verify the producer's allowed kind, version, role, and owner domain before append. Only application_origin producers may emit authoritative application effects. Fixture telemetry, subjects, connectors, importers, and manual observers cannot manufacture submission commitment or identity verification. The server provenance label alone does not establish an application fact. derivation: "An HTTP 200, an accepted telemetry packet, and authentication are different facts." x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part VI; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§3.3, 5.3, 10.3."
- id: EK-OBSERVATION classification: invariant rule: >- Producer IDs identify one sequence lifetime. Deduplicate identical (producer_id, producer_sequence) deliveries without duplicating effects. Conflicting content under that key is an integrity incident, not last-write-wins. Journal gaps, overflow, loss, flush receipts, and producer closure. A closed HTTP connection is not producer completeness or execution termination. consequence: >- A complete producer assessment requires an evidenced terminal sequence and no unresolved gap. Late evidence appends at the current head and produces a new diagnostic revision, never a silent repair of the old revision. derivation: "Silence cannot distinguish successful termination from lost observation." x-status: inferred x-source: *d
- id: EK-NULL classification: invariant rule: >- Every null is Missing(value=null, reason=). Empty arrays mean an established empty collection, not unknown contents. Unknown semantic states remain explicit enums; false and zero are never missing-value sentinels. manual_override requires an authenticated journaled operator decision and preserves the superseded observation. derivation: "Ambiguous missingness becomes an integration bug." x-status: extracted x-source: *h
- id: EK-TIME classification: invariant rule: >- Every Measurement and TimePoint identifies its origin, clock, and boot. Register clocks in the manifest or a clock_registered event. Persist monotonic offsets relative to that boot. A clock_registered event may atomically introduce the clock used for its own receipt timestamp. Never subtract across clock IDs or boots. UTC is annotation only. consequence: >- For endpoint_difference, both endpoints must match the measurement's clock, boot, and origin; end must be at least start, and estimate.value must equal end minus start. A bounded estimate has at least one numeric bound and lower_bound <= upper_bound when both exist. Duration values and bounds are nonnegative. Exact zero is valid. derivation: "The diagnosed circus-tent _elapsed() zero defect demonstrates the failure." x-status: extracted x-source: *h
- id: EK-TIMING-INTERPRETATION classification: invariant rule: >- Exact describes the recorded value at its declared origin, not its truth across origins. Preserve subject reports unchanged. Assign an opaque report clock when native clock coordinates are unavailable; do not invent native endpoints. Compare independently derived durations only for matching semantic boundaries or an evidenced bound. A comparability_group name alone is insufficient. Never divide aggregate runtime into invented step durations. consequence: >- Harness deadlines, native timeouts, browser elapsed time, server elapsed time, and manual stopwatch references remain separate observations. Observation loss yields bounds or unavailable, not an exact truncated duration. derivation: "A harness timeout is not a native timeout; unlike intervals cannot establish a timing lie." x-status: inferred x-source: "3-hellscape-blueprint.md §4.5; 5-browser-qualification.md."
- id: EK-CAPABILITY classification: invariant rule: >- A descriptor applies to exactly one subject_id, subject_version, configured mode, and interface surface. Its catalog must enumerate every capability for that scope. Every new subject version starts unknown until its own evidence establishes another availability. Omission and predecessor descriptors do not imply inheritance, presence, or absence. consequence: >- Scope every cited capability to the assessed version. A non-unknown availability requires journaled evidence and limitations. Documentation may support a declaration but not a run-success finding. A harness watchdog cannot establish native cancellation; fixture namespacing cannot establish browser isolation; unsupported connector mapping is not native absence. derivation: "Version inheritance converts a prior finding into an untested assumption." x-status: extracted x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part VI; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §4.3."
- id: EK-ASSESSMENT classification: invariant rule: >- Capability, opportunity, and result are independent fields. satisfied or violated requires a valid exposed opportunity, applicable controls, and supporting evidence. native_absence requires a required, evidenced absent native capability in the exact scope, not mere failure to reach a step. Unexposed work is not_exercised; blocked or invalidly controlled work is not_exercised or indeterminate according to what was actually observed. consequence: >- A capability may be absent while its unexercised facet remains not_exercised. Invalid isolation write controls cannot establish non-isolation. A missing dependency is an infrastructure/prerequisite finding, not a driver failure. A skipped required step is not a pass. derivation: "A single availability/outcome enum cannot represent these cases without losing evidence." x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part VI; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§1.3, 4; 5-browser-qualification.md."
- id: EK-CLAIMS classification: invariant rule: >- Preserve claim source, semantic scope, receipt time, and knowledge boundary. None, protocol acknowledgement, HTTP success, and execution completion do not establish application commitment. Authentication and correlation are independent checks. A valid signature with a trace mismatch remains authenticated but not reliably correlated to the claimed attempt. consequence: >- The analyzer compares claims with authoritative postconditions without rewriting either. Close-time outcome-unknown is not contradicted by later commitment. A definite no-commit/cancel claim may be contradicted by later correlated commitment. Forced termination and fixture sealing are not native cancellation or rollback. derivation: "The cancellation observations require distinct claim, effect, close, and reconciliation facts." x-status: extracted x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part VI; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§4.6, 5.3–5.5."
- id: EK-ATTEMPT-SCOPE classification: invariant rule: >- An application attempt has immutable kind at commissioning. A laboratory fixture is practice and held_in. An employer origin is held_out; production requires an employer origin. derived_from references only the same kind. rehearsal_of links practice to production; performance_of links production to practice. These are lineage links, never evidence promotion. consequence: >- Production postconditions may not cite practice commitment as proof of production commitment. Imported historical qualification material is historical_unscored. Real job content used in a fixture does not make fixture forms origin-representative. derivation: "Tuning against Hellscape cannot qualify an executor for an untested employer form." x-status: extracted x-source: *b
- id: EK-MANUAL classification: invariant rule: >- Manual execution has no automation subject, connector version, or binding version. It may produce genuine production observations and origin receipts. Human actions and notes retain manual provenance and disclosed assistance. An operator note alone cannot set an authoritative business predicate. consequence: >- In manual fixture validation, subject requirement facets are not_exercised, with rationale manual_fixture_validation. Do not fabricate a subject capability descriptor or credit a browser framework with human completion. No automation or laboratory dependency is required to admit the manual run. derivation: "Human assistance is not unattended completion; the system must produce applications before its infrastructure is finished." x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Parts VII–IX; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§4.4, 11.1, 12; 5-browser-qualification.md."
- id: EK-DIAGNOSTIC classification: invariant rule: >- A diagnostic is a deterministic function of its immutable manifest, named journal prefix, and pinned classifier bundle. The bundle includes requirement and optional fix registries. It uses no current wall time, unrecorded network lookups, or mutable application rows as additional evidence. consequence: >- Its prefix ends at its analysis_requested event, which pins diagnostic ID, analysis revision, and analysis versions. All copied observations and evidence references must be supported by that prefix. Corrections, late evidence, or classifier changes create a new request and immutable revision. Readable reports render this same object. derivation: "Replay must be re-derivation, not reproduction of an edited report." x-status: inferred x-source: *d
- id: EK-REPLAY classification: invariant rule: >- Exact fixture replay consumes recorded external inputs and lifecycle observations, recomputes derived outputs, and compares semantic events, final state, and the diagnostic. It must not feed recorded derived outputs back as authoritative inputs. Diagnostic-only replay may re-derive a production diagnostic, but cannot replay an employer mutation. consequence: >- Replay invokes no browser, subject, or external write. Recorded timing is input; replay does not sleep to simulate it. matched requires every mode-required comparison to be available and equal. Missing inputs cannot yield matched. Live reproduction is a new attempt, not an exact replay. derivation: "Identical fixture inputs can reproduce fixture semantics, not unknown live browser behavior." x-status: extracted x-source: *f
- id: EK-LEASE classification: invariant rule: >- Claim atomically checks eligible resource state and absence of an unexpired lease, assigns a unique fencing lease_id and owner epoch, advances the entity revision, clears last_failure_reason, and appends evidence without changing resource_state. Completion checks lease ID, unexpired authority-clock deadline, entity/input revisions, and applicable owner/session epochs. A rejected stale completion has no effect. consequence: >- Release, expiry, and confirmed-death recovery clear ownership atomically. A failed claim generation increments its entity retry_count at most once. If retries remain, preserve the pending state; otherwise apply the owner's terminal route and dead-letter occurrence with its reason or retry_exhausted. A successful completion is not a failed retry. derivation: "Lease ownership is orthogonal to queue state; duplicated reclamation must not consume retries twice." x-status: extracted x-source: *l
- id: EK-LEASE-RESTART classification: proposed_mechanism rule: >- leased_at and lease_expires_at use one registered lease-authority clock and boot; expiry must be later than issue. Renewal requires a still-current token and epoch. On authority restart, durably fence the old authority epoch before reclaiming its leases. Never compare old offsets with the new boot, and never infer elapsed downtime from UTC. consequence: >- Reclamation revokes local commit authority, not proof that a worker or external application stopped. Recovery of a side-effecting attempt must retain outcome uncertainty until separately reconciled. rationale: "This preserves monotonic timing without relying on Stage1 A5's unverified skew bound." flip_condition: >- Replace epoch invalidation with a durable external lease clock only after that authority's persistence and comparison semantics pass the same fencing and restart corpus. x-status: proposed x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part VI; 2-state-bank-crawler-blueprint.json A5 and §11.15."
- id: EK-ARTIFACTS classification: invariant rule: >- Citable artifacts are immutable, content-addressed, access-classified, and registered by journal events. Retain bytes while a retained manifest, journal prefix, diagnostic, replay bundle, or archive depends on them. Do not substitute a locator or hash alone for promised archived content. consequence: >- Credentials and session secrets do not enter ordinary journal payloads. Restricted native bodies and personal application receipts use controlled artifact storage. If bytes are lost, preserve their known identity and append observation_lost; never silently replace them or claim exact replay. derivation: "A durable evidence reference to absent or mutable bytes is not durable evidence." x-status: inferred x-source: "2-state-bank-crawler-blueprint.json §11 and Decision 8; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§10.1–10.2; 6-get-a-job.xml.txt AGENTS.md."
x-open-evidence: - missing: >- The raw cancellation-fixed.jsonl, isolation-fixed.jsonl, FINDINGS-v2.md, native response bodies, and executable legacy schemas are not included. resolution: >- Import available originals with checksums, source scope, and historical classification. Until then, retain the blueprint's descriptions as documentary evidence, not newly executed or current-version observations. This is not a pre-M1 or production-application gate. x-status: uncertain x-source: "3-hellscape-blueprint.md §1.3 names these artifacts but does not supply their bytes."
oneOf: - $ref: "#/$defs/Manifest" - $ref: "#/$defs/JournalEnvelope" - $ref: "#/$defs/DiagnosticDocument" - $ref: "#/$defs/ReplayReceipt" - $ref: "#/$defs/LeaseRecord" - $ref: "#/$defs/CapabilityDescriptor"
$defs: SchemaVersion: const: evidence-kernel/0.1.0 x-status: proposed x-source: *w
Identifier: type: string minLength: 1 description: Opaque identifier; no identity, authority, or ordering is inferred from its spelling. x-status: inferred x-source: *s
Revision: type: integer minimum: 0 maximum: 9007199254740991 x-status: proposed x-source: *w
PositiveInteger: type: integer minimum: 1 maximum: 9007199254740991 x-status: proposed x-source: *w
NonNegativeNumber: type: number minimum: 0 x-status: extracted x-source: *h
Digest: type: string pattern: '^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$' x-status: proposed x-source: *w
NullReason: type: string enum: - not_enabled - not_applicable - not_observed - observation_lost - unsupported_by_subject - manual_override x-status: extracted x-source: *h x-meanings: not_enabled: The facility or analysis was deliberately disabled. not_applicable: The field has no meaning in this declared scope. not_observed: The value was not established by observation. observation_lost: An expected or previously available observation is unavailable through loss. unsupported_by_subject: The subject lacks the scoped native facility needed to supply this value. manual_override: An authenticated operator explicitly withheld or superseded the value.
Missing: type: object additionalProperties: false required: [value, reason] properties: value: {type: "null", x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} reason: {$ref: "#/$defs/NullReason", x-status: extracted, x-source: *h} detail: {type: string, minLength: 1, x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} x-status: proposed x-source: *w
Inapplicable: allOf: - $ref: "#/$defs/Missing" - properties: reason: {const: not_applicable, x-status: extracted, x-source: *h} x-status: proposed x-source: *w
MaybeString: oneOf: - $ref: "#/$defs/Identifier" - $ref: "#/$defs/Missing" x-status: proposed x-source: *w
MaybeDigest: oneOf: - $ref: "#/$defs/Digest" - $ref: "#/$defs/Missing" x-status: proposed x-source: *w
MaybeNumber: oneOf: - type: number - $ref: "#/$defs/Missing" x-status: proposed x-source: *w
MaybeNonNegative: oneOf: - $ref: "#/$defs/NonNegativeNumber" - $ref: "#/$defs/Missing" x-status: proposed x-source: *w
MaybeBoolean: oneOf: - type: boolean - $ref: "#/$defs/Missing" x-status: proposed x-source: *w
EvidenceValue: anyOf: - type: string - type: number - type: boolean - $ref: "#/$defs/Missing" - type: array items: {$ref: "#/$defs/EvidenceValue"} - $ref: "#/$defs/EvidenceMap" description: JSON evidence values with reasoned nulls at every nesting depth. x-status: proposed x-source: *w
EvidenceMap: type: object additionalProperties: {$ref: "#/$defs/EvidenceValue"} x-status: proposed x-source: *w
Scope: type: object additionalProperties: false required: [kind, id] properties: kind: type: string enum: [run, session, connector_call, workflow_step, application_operation, native_primitive, recovery, discovery, capability, resource] x-status: proposed x-source: *d id: {$ref: "#/$defs/Identifier", x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} x-status: proposed x-source: *w
EvidenceRef: type: object additionalProperties: false required: [journal_id, sequence, event_id, event_hash, pointer] properties: journal_id: {$ref: "#/$defs/Identifier", x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} sequence: {$ref: "#/$defs/PositiveInteger", x-status: inferred, x-source: *d} event_id: {$ref: "#/$defs/Identifier", x-status: extracted, x-source: *d} event_hash: {$ref: "#/$defs/Digest", x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} pointer: type: string pattern: '^(?:/(?:[^~/]|~[01])*)*$' description: JSON Pointer; empty string cites the entire event. x-status: proposed x-source: *w x-status: proposed x-source: *w
EvidenceRefs: type: array items: {$ref: "#/$defs/EvidenceRef"} uniqueItems: true x-status: proposed x-source: *w
SupportRefs: allOf: - $ref: "#/$defs/EvidenceRefs" - minItems: 1 x-status: inferred x-source: *h
JournalPrefix: type: object additionalProperties: false required: [journal_id, last_sequence, head_hash] properties: journal_id: {$ref: "#/$defs/Identifier", x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} last_sequence: {$ref: "#/$defs/PositiveInteger", x-status: inferred, x-source: *d} head_hash: {$ref: "#/$defs/Digest", x-status: inferred, x-source: *d} description: A nonempty, immutable prefix; admission is its first event. x-status: proposed x-source: *w
ArtifactReference: type: object additionalProperties: false required: [digest, size_bytes, media_type, owner_domain, access] properties: digest: {$ref: "#/$defs/Digest", x-status: inferred, x-source: *d} size_bytes: {$ref: "#/$defs/Revision", x-status: inferred, x-source: *d} media_type: {$ref: "#/$defs/Identifier", x-status: inferred, x-source: *d} owner_domain: {$ref: "#/$defs/Identifier", x-status: inferred, x-source: *s} access: enum: [public, restricted] x-status: proposed x-source: *w description: >- Immutable byte identity, not a credential-bearing URL. The owner's resolver supplies a locator. Possession of this reference grants no read authority. x-status: proposed x-source: *w
ArtifactSlot: type: object additionalProperties: false required: [name, expected_digest, content, evidence_refs] properties: name: {$ref: "#/$defs/Identifier", x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} expected_digest: {$ref: "#/$defs/MaybeDigest", x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} content: oneOf: - $ref: "#/$defs/ArtifactReference" - $ref: "#/$defs/Missing" x-status: inferred x-source: *d evidence_refs: {$ref: "#/$defs/SupportRefs", x-status: inferred, x-source: *h} description: >- Missing retrieval does not erase an already known digest. If content exists, expected_digest must equal content.digest. x-status: proposed x-source: *w
VersionPin: type: object additionalProperties: false required: [id, version, artifact_digest] properties: id: {$ref: "#/$defs/Identifier", x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} version: {$ref: "#/$defs/Identifier", x-status: extracted, x-source: *d} artifact_digest: {$ref: "#/$defs/Digest", x-status: extracted, x-source: *d} description: A known immutable code, schema, policy, catalog, or registry artifact. x-status: inferred x-source: *d
MeasurementOrigin: enum: [engine_measured, browser_measured, subject_reported, manual_reference] x-status: extracted x-source: *d
ClockDescriptor: type: object additionalProperties: false required: [clock_id, boot_id, origin, source_id, basis, unit] properties: clock_id: {$ref: "#/$defs/Identifier", x-status: extracted, x-source: *h} boot_id: {$ref: "#/$defs/Identifier", x-status: inferred, x-source: *h} origin: {$ref: "#/$defs/MeasurementOrigin", x-status: extracted, x-source: *d} source_id: {$ref: "#/$defs/Identifier", x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} basis: enum: [monotonic_offset, opaque_report] x-status: proposed x-source: *w unit: {const: ms, x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} description: >- An opaque-report clock identifies a reporting source and its lifetime, not a known native monotonic epoch. A browser document gets a new clock lifetime on document replacement. x-status: inferred x-source: *d
TimePoint: type: object additionalProperties: false required: [clock_id, boot_id, origin, monotonic_offset_ms, utc_annotation] properties: clock_id: {$ref: "#/$defs/Identifier", x-status: extracted, x-source: *h} boot_id: {$ref: "#/$defs/Identifier", x-status: inferred, x-source: *h} origin: {$ref: "#/$defs/MeasurementOrigin", x-status: extracted, x-source: *h} monotonic_offset_ms: {$ref: "#/$defs/NonNegativeNumber", x-status: inferred, x-source: *d} utc_annotation: oneOf: - type: string format: date-time - $ref: "#/$defs/Missing" x-status: extracted x-source: *h description: >- A coordinate in a registered monotonic clock. $schema: https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema $id: urn:job-application:contracts:application-attempt-lifecycle:0.1.0 title: Application attempt lifecycle description: >- Review draft for commissioning, observing, and reconciling one application attempt without collapsing dispatch, observation, execution claims, origin facts, and reporting into a single status. x-contract: name: application-attempt-lifecycle version: 0.1.0 maturity: review_draft owner: contracts consumers: [job-hunter, Circus Tent, Ringmaster, Hellscape] conformance_suite: conformance/01-application-attempt-lifecycle.md corpus: - qualification_evidence_discipline - cancellation_and_late_commitment_cases - synthetic_connector_lifecycle_cases - manual_practice_and_production_recording purpose: >- Track the candidate's attempts through honest outcomes, including unresolved outcomes, and retain the evidence needed to improve execution. x-kernel-compatibility: version: evidence-kernel/0.1.0 reference_policy: >- All schema references are local. The common definitions below preserve the kernel's wire meanings; this file does not introduce alternative null, timing, digest, provenance, or evidence-reference conventions. mirrored_types: - Identifier - Revision - PositiveInteger - Digest - Missing - EvidenceRef - JournalPrefix - ArtifactReference - VersionPin - TimePoint - Measurement - MeasurementEvidence - SubjectIdentity - AssistanceRecord - AttemptContext application_restriction: >- ExecutionDescriptor is restricted to manual or subject for an application attempt. The kernel's service mode remains valid for discovery and other non-application work. validation_gate: >- Structural validation and all LIFE rules are required. Validate evidence references, identities, ownership, publication revisions, and measurements against retained kernel evidence; a structurally valid source_checks object is not itself proof that its checks occurred. x-status: proposed x-source: *k
x-ownership: commissioning: authority: commissioner scope: >- Immutable candidate, job, task, permission, execution configuration, lineage, and owner bindings. This is metadata, not a sixth outcome axis. x-status: inferred x-source: *h dispatch: authority: connector scope: Intended delivery, local handle, delivery uncertainty, and native acceptance evidence. x-status: extracted x-source: *h observation: authority: connector scope: >- Observation window, local deadlines, connection closure, bounded drain, cleanup observations, and the immutable close-time knowledge snapshot. x-status: inferred x-source: *d execution: authority: subject scope: >- Subject-authored claims only. An authenticated adapter may faithfully publish them for the bound subject; it may not invent or strengthen them. x-status: inferred x-source: *h application: authority: origin scope: >- Origin facts only. Hellscape's reducer supplies practice facts; a production receipt gateway records verified facts from the bound employer origin without becoming the origin or the reconciler. x-status: proposed x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part VI; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§3.2, 4.6, 11.1." report: authority: reconciler scope: >- Comparisons and limitations over pinned source revisions. Dispatch and execution remain explicitly inapplicable. Manual actions are observations, not fabricated subject claims; employer receipt evidence can still establish an application fact. x-status: proposed x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part IX; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§3.1, 4.4, 11.1."

Product projections may retain their own workflow fields, but must cite these independently owned axes. x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part VI; 2-state-bank-crawler-blueprint.json §11.14; 6-get-a-job.xml.txt docs/contracts/firestore-collections.md." - decision: >- Native /run completed maps initially to an execution-lifecycle claim, not application commitment. Primitive success, acknowledgement, and None never acquire stronger semantics merely through normalization. x-status: extracted x-source: "3-hellscape-blueprint.md §4.6; 5-browser-qualification.md." - decision: >- Execution and application domains retain cumulative immutable claim/fact histories. Receipt order is not assumed to be occurrence order, and a later callback cannot silently replace an earlier conflicting response. x-status: proposed x-source: *d - decision: >- Report.state has only reconciled and contradicted as decided verdicts. Missing with reason represents no decidable or applicable verdict; it is not a third success state. Reconciled means the declared comparisons were accounted for, not that the application succeeded or every native claim was independently proved. x-status: proposed x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part VI; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§4.4–4.6." - decision: >- A production origin need not implement this portfolio's connector or journal API. x-invariants: - id: LIFE-COMMISSION classification: invariant rule: >- Commission before an authorized automated dispatch. Freeze attempt identity, kind, candidate, job snapshot, target, task, execution configuration, owner bindings, and permissions. The commission must agree with the admitted manifest and be journaled before Start can cause a native request. Changing the subject version, target, kind, or task creates a new attempt. derivation: "A later outcome cannot determine retroactively what was commissioned." x-status: inferred x-source: *h
- id: LIFE-AXES classification: invariant rule: >- Exactly one authority role owns each of the five axes. Each applicable axis has exactly one bound publication writer. A writer may publish only its axis and must preserve the identity of its authoritative source. A report writer must not hold execution/application write authority. No whole-attempt status or multi-axis update command is defined here. consequence: >- Missing source evidence is not permission for another owner to fill the axis. An inapplicable manual execution axis has no invented subject or active subject writer. derivation: "A single status cannot represent connection closure, unknown execution, and later commitment." x-status: extracted x-source: *h
- id: LIFE-PUBLICATION classification: invariant rule: >- Axis revisions are complete immutable publications. The key is (attempt_id, kind, axis, revision); a different value under the same key is an integrity conflict. Each next revision is previous_revision + 1. Only the owner-local revision check and journal commit are atomic. Publication to readers is asynchronous and cannot require another owner's transaction, acknowledgement, or payload serialization. consequence: >- A snapshot pins one complete publication per axis, or revision zero for no publication. Readers see old-or-new publications, never partial bodies. A snapshot seal records the locally available version vector, not global synchronous linearizability. derivation: "Stage1's independent write domains must survive composition of the attempt record." x-status: inferred x-source: *o
- id: LIFE-EVIDENCE classification: invariant rule: >- The journal is the source of truth. Every publication cites its supporting prefix and source evidence; it is itself registered after its bytes exist. Do not put the publication's own registration event or digest inside its derivation inputs. Imported evidence must be registered locally with its original scope and trust, not promoted by the act of import. consequence: >- Readers verify commission digests, owner identity, evidence references, artifact availability, and prefix bounds before using a publication. Synthetic and historical-unscored records cannot count as real production applications. derivation: "Anything added outside the journal could otherwise become retroactive evidence." x-status: inferred x-source: *h
- id: LIFE-DISPATCH classification: invariant rule: >- Prepare is non-executing. Before the first native delivery, durably allocate the connector-local handle and record the intended request digest, idempotency key, and dispatching transition. A native run ID is attached only when actually received and correlated. Local Start acknowledgement is not native acceptance; native acceptance is not execution completion. consequence: >- A crash or lost response around delivery yields uncertain unless stronger evidence establishes acceptance or non-acceptance. A local prerequisite or translation failure is not a fabricated subject execution failure. derivation: "Acknowledgement, execution, and semantic success have different evidence boundaries." x-status: inferred x-source: "3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§5.2–5.4 and 10.6; 5-browser-qualification.md."
- id: LIFE-IDEMPOTENCY classification: invariant rule: >- The commissioning idempotency key is scoped to the commissioning principal and immutable attempt request. Same key and request returns the same local attempt/handle; changed content under the key is rejected. Repeated Start does not launch a second logical execution. consequence: >- Native resend/resume requires an evidenced native idempotency or checkpoint contract, matching request identity, and a journaled recovery authorization. It remains the same logical delivery and cannot re-execute a completed side-effecting step. Without those guarantees, preserve uncertainty and require reconciliation or explicit duplicate-risk review before a new try. A local lease expiry does not establish safe resubmission. derivation: "A local ledger cannot roll back an employer write whose acknowledgement was lost." x-status: inferred x-source: "3-hellscape-blueprint.md §10.6; 4-circus-tent-arch.md §5.6."
- id: LIFE-CLOSE classification: invariant rule: >- Active observation, transport connection, native execution, application mutation authority, and native context lifetime are distinct. On the local active deadline or end request, stop issuing workflow commands, record native-cancel availability and any attempt, record transport closure, and drain effects/evidence only within the commissioned bound. consequence: >- Close the observation window even if the subject continues. Freeze the close-time knowledge snapshot and version pins. Later evidence may append and revise the report but cannot reopen that window, rewrite close-time knowledge, or silently resume workflow commands. derivation: "The observed post-disconnect continuation makes close equivalent to cancel unsound." x-status: extracted x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part VI; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §5.5."
- id: LIFE-CONTROLS classification: invariant rule: >- RequestNativeCancel, CloseObservationConnection, ReleaseNativeContext, and Contain are separately evidenced operations. A request is not an acknowledgement; acknowledgement is not an observed effect. A stop claim is retained as a subject claim, not upgraded to a no-commit fact. consequence: >- Unsupported or uncertain cancellation does not prevent local finalization. Containment needs explicit authority and records its affected scope. Killing a process, releasing a context, quarantining a slot, or sealing a fixture does not demonstrate subject-native bounded cancellation or undo committed application work. derivation: "Forced termination is not cooperative cancellation, and application transactions can outlive a client." x-status: extracted x-source: "3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§4.1, 5.5, 13; 5-browser-qualification.md."
- id: LIFE-CLAIMS classification: invariant rule: >- Execution publications contain only faithfully mapped, source-attributed claims from the commissioned subject/version. Preserve raw responses, mapping versions, declared scope, original times when available, and receipt times. An absent state is Missing, not an invented subject claim of unknown. Explicit unknown remains a valid subject claim. consequence: >- Append conflicting authenticated responses/callbacks without last-write-wins replacement. A terminal-looking claim does not prohibit recording later conflicting evidence. Primitive or lifecycle scope is not silently widened to application commitment. derivation: "The reconciler must compare the original claim, not a corrected copy of it." x-status: inferred x-source: *d
- id: LIFE-ORIGIN classification: invariant rule: >- An application fact must identify the commissioned origin, candidate, job, and attempt, and cite verified source and correlation evidence under the pinned origin policy. A local fixture fact cites its transaction; a production fact cites an actual verified origin receipt. HTTP 200, a submit click, a subject result, or an operator assertion alone is insufficient. consequence: >- No accepted fact means unknown knowledge, not not_committed. An as-of absence permits later commitment. Final absence requires an origin-owned guarantee covering the attempt, not expiration of the observer's timer. A valid commitment remains historical evidence even after withdrawal, employer rejection, job closure, or lost confirmation rendering. derivation: "Execution is a subject claim; application commitment is an origin fact." x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part VI; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§4.6, 9.3, 11.1."
- id: LIFE-SOURCE-CHECKS classification: invariant rule: >- Verify source identity and attempt correlation independently. Preserve trace mismatch separately from authentication. An authenticated but uncorrelated message remains evidence of receipt, not an accepted claim/fact for an arbitrary attempt. Strong alternate correlation may establish the attempt despite a trace defect, but must be explicit and evidenced. consequence: >- Normalization metadata is assigned by the authenticated ingestion/verification path, never accepted merely because the sender serialized verified or matched. Native receipt IDs and versions are never invented. derivation: "A valid signature and a matching trace describe different properties." x-status: inferred x-source: "3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§1.3 and 5.3."
- id: LIFE-RECONCILE classification: invariant rule: >- The reconciler reads pinned execution claims and origin facts and writes only report. Compare propositions at their actual scope and knowledge boundary. A stopped claim alone does not assert that an already dispatched origin transaction cannot commit. consequence: >- Close-time outcome_unknown is compatible with a later commitment. A claim that no commitment occurred anywhere in the attempt is contradicted by a valid commitment for that attempt. A claim limited to an earlier boundary is not contradicted merely because a receipt arrived later. derivation: "The cancellation corpus distinguishes honest uncertainty from a definite false cancellation guarantee." x-status: extracted x-source: *h
- id: LIFE-REPORT-COVERAGE classification: proposed_mechanism rule: >- Every claim and application assertion in the pinned execution publication is accounted for by a comparison or an explicit scope/uncertainty limitation. Any proved contradiction makes report.state contradicted, even if other comparisons remain incomplete. With no contradiction, complete comparisons yield reconciled; unresolved comparisons yield Missing with reason. No applicable subject claims yield not_applicable coverage, not a fabricated successful comparison. consequence: >- not_comparable can be a complete scope determination, such as execution completion making no application claim. It is not proof of the claim's truth. Consumers must display coverage and limitations with the verdict. rationale: "A binary decided verdict must not turn undecidable evidence into a pass." flip_condition: >- Revise the representation only if corpus cases cannot distinguish a decided comparison from incomplete or inapplicable comparison without another explicitly versioned field; never weaken the claim/fact separation. x-status: proposed x-source: *w
- id: LIFE-LATE-EVIDENCE classification: invariant rule: >- Evidence received after observation closure is appended at the current journal head. Publish new owner revisions and a new report over new input pins; preserve every prior seal, publication, and diagnostic. A current snapshot may legitimately contain newer facts than its latest report used. consequence: >- Report freshness is determined by comparing its input pins with the snapshot's source pins. A stale report is not silently applied to newer facts, and publication does not wait for synchronous reconciliation. derivation: "Asynchronous publication and immutable close-time knowledge must both remain true." x-status: inferred x-source: "2-state-bank-crawler-blueprint.json Decision 8; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§5.5 and 10.7."
- id: LIFE-LINEAGE classification: invariant rule: >- kind is immutable. Laboratory fixtures are practice and held_in; employer origins are held_out and production requires an employer origin. derived_from is same-kind and acyclic. rehearsal_of points from practice to an already commissioned production identity; performance_of points from production to an already commissioned practice identity. consequence: >- Empty arrays are valid. Reciprocal mutation of an earlier commission is not required: readers can derive incoming links. Links establish lineage, not inherited commitment, native capability, or origin representativeness. Practice success never triggers production dispatch automatically. derivation: "Practice-as-production reproduces the laboratory overfitting failure." x-status: inferred x-source: *s
- id: LIFE-MANUAL classification: invariant rule: >- Manual mode requires no automation subject, native run ID, connector version, or native binding version. Its dispatch and execution slots stay at revision zero with not_applicable. The recorder owns observation and journals human actions with manual provenance. consequence: >- The origin fact recorder can accept a separately verified employer receipt. The reconciler does not manufacture a subject claim to compare with it. A real application with pending confirmation remains a tracked attempt; absence of infrastructure is not a reason to lose its evidence. derivation: "Human assistance is not unattended completion, but manual work must serve the portfolio from day one." x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Parts VII–IX; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §4.4; 5-browser-qualification.md."
- id: LIFE-TIME classification: invariant rule: >- All measured durations use Measurement with clock_id, boot_id, origin, discriminated estimate, and censoring. Endpoint subtraction requires one registered clock/boot/origin and ordered endpoints; exact zero is valid. UTC annotations and receipt order cannot establish cross-clock occurrence order. Opaque origin revisions are not lexically ordered as timestamps. consequence: >- A restart interrupts the old observation epoch; do not reconstruct elapsed downtime by subtracting new-boot offsets or UTC. Configured DurationLimit values are declarations, not measurements or native capability evidence. derivation: "The zero-duration defect and restart ambiguity require explicit timing provenance." x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part VI; contracts/00-evidence-kernel.yaml."
x-transition-rules: dispatch: states: [not_started, prepared, dispatching, accepted, rejected, uncertain] allowed: - {from: unpublished, to: [not_started, prepared, rejected]} - {from: not_started, to: [prepared, rejected]} - {from: prepared, to: [dispatching, rejected]} - {from: dispatching, to: [accepted, rejected, uncertain]} - {from: uncertain, to: [uncertain, accepted, rejected]} - {from: accepted, to: [accepted]} - {from: rejected, to: [rejected]} guards: - "dispatching requires durable local handle, request identity, and dispatch intent before wire delivery." - "accepted requires correlated native acceptance/result evidence, not merely local Start acknowledgement." - "rejected after possible delivery requires evidence of native non-acceptance; a lost response is uncertain." - "Same-state revisions may add evidence but cannot authorize a new logical execution." - "Authorized same-key native resume preserves accepted as the logical dispatch state and journals every additional delivery." - "Manual dispatch has no state transition; its slot is explicitly inapplicable." x-status: proposed x-source: *w
observation: states: [not_opened, open, draining, closed] allowed: - {from: unpublished, to: [not_opened, open, closed]} - {from: not_opened, to: [open, closed]} - {from: open, to: [open, draining, closed]} - {from: draining, to: [draining, closed]} - {from: closed, to: [closed]} guards: - "A closed-first publication is allowed for translation, launch, or infrastructure failure." - "Transport closure can occur while the observation window is open or draining." - "closed requires a journaled closure boundary and a close-time knowledge snapshot." - "closed-to-closed may append late observations or cleanup evidence but preserves the original closure fields." - "Active/drain/cleanup waiting must remain within the commissioned local bounds." x-status: proposed x-source: *w
execution: rule: >- Append authenticated, correlated claims. Do not impose a truth-state machine on what a subject is allowed to claim: a contradictory claim is evidence to retain, not a reason to replace or suppress the previous claim. Existing claim IDs and contents cannot change. x-status: inferred x-source: *d
application: rule: >- Append accepted, correlated origin facts; existing fact IDs and contents cannot change. An as-of absence and later commitment can both be valid. Apparently conflicting final facts or multiple origin commitments require explicit report issues and preserved evidence, never latest-value erasure. x-status: proposed x-source: *w
report: rule: >- Publish new immutable assessments. Input revision pins must not regress relative to this report domain's previous publication. Historical replay may reproduce old reports as artifacts without replacing the current report domain. New facts may make a prior report stale or a prior reconciled verdict contradicted; prior bytes remain intact. x-status: proposed x-source: *w
x-reconciler-algorithm: steps: - >- Verify the commission, source owner publications, source checks, all input pins, and their journal support. Retain unresolved source conflicts as issues; do not repair an input axis. - >- Enumerate the subject claims and each explicit application assertion from the pinned execution revision. A primitive or lifecycle claim without an application assertion receives not_comparable with its narrow scope stated. - >- Match application facts only to the same attempt, kind, target, candidate, and job. Establish temporal relation using a common clock, evidenced causality, or a documented origin sequence; otherwise record unknown. - >- Compare explicit outcome_unknown with known facts as compatible uncertainty, not a prediction of no future commitment. Later commitment alone never contradicts it. If no relevant fact is available, preserve indeterminacy. - >- Compare committed with a matching positive fact or an authoritative absence covering the claimed interval. An earlier as-of absence cannot disprove later commitment, and absence of a receipt cannot prove non-commitment. - >- Compare not_committed over entire_attempt against any verified commitment for that attempt. For at_boundary or after_boundary, require temporal evidence covering that boundary; a later receipt timestamp alone is insufficient. Verification of a future no-commit guarantee requires origin-owned finality, not local observation closure. - >- Produce comparisons, coverage, issues, and the decided or reasoned-missing report state. Publish only the report domain and any separately derived diagnostic artifact, preserving all source records. x-status: proposed x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part VI; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§4.5–4.6."
x-open-evidence: - missing: >- The sources do not provide current per-origin production receipt, authentication, correlation, or final-absence mappings. resolution: >- Pin each admitted origin's mapping from documented semantics and retained, operator-authorized receipt observations. Until established, retain raw observations and leave application knowledge unresolved; do not require this reconnaissance for unrelated jobs or manual recording. x-status: uncertain x-source: "3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§4.6 and 11.1; 6-get-a-job.xml.txt docs/external/README.md." - missing: >- Raw historical cancellation artifacts and a current-version native cancellation/cleanup contract are not supplied. resolution: >- Preserve historical descriptions as unscored documentary evidence, and test lifecycle behavior with synthetic backends. A new subject version starts unknown until its own capability evidence is collected. x-status: uncertain x-source: "3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§1.3, 4.3, 5.3."

$schema: https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema $id: urn:job-application:contracts:external-connector:0.1.0 title: External connector description: >- Review draft of the shared asynchronous, task-shaped interface used to commission browser execution and discovery work, observe its evidence, and control local exposure without confusing observation closure with native cancellation. Circus Tent and Ringmaster implement this interface independently. All schema references are local to this file. x-status: proposed x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt, Parts III, V, VI, and VIII."

Message discriminators, identifiers, pagination, limits, and transport mechanics are proposals, not claims about deployed native interfaces.
x-contract: name: external-connector version: 0.1.0 maturity: review_draft owner: contracts consumers: [crawler, Circus Tent, Ringmaster, Hellscape, job-hunter] conformance_suite: conformance/02-external-connector.md reference_corpus: Hellscape_M1_synthetic_backends implementation_status: specified_not_certified purpose: >- Let job-hunter commission real applications through either executor and collect evidence from every attempt. Let discovery use the same task/control mechanics without inventing application attempts. Manual applications use the evidence kernel and lifecycle directly; an automation connector is not a prerequisite for recording them. x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Parts VI–IX; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§5 and 10.6."
x-compatibility: kernel_version: evidence-kernel/0.1.0 lifecycle_version: application-attempt-lifecycle/0.1.0 rules: - >- Common evidence, timing, capability, assistance, source-check, claim, and control-observation definitions preserve their established wire meanings. A connector response is not itself a kernel journal envelope. - >- Lifecycle publications are carried by typed immutable references, not whole-attempt updates. Their complete bytes retain the lifecycle schema version. This connector does not redefine their five-owner composition. - >- binding_version in an application execution descriptor identifies the external native-interface mapping version, corresponding here to ConfigurationPin.binding.version. A browser's internal binding identity belongs in the subject's stack; it is not a shared primitive protocol. - >- Validate JSON Schema and every applicable EXT rule. Unknown versions, duplicate mapping keys, non-finite numbers, unknown closed-object fields, and bare normalized nulls are rejected. Enforce date-time and URI formats. x-status: proposed x-source: "contracts/00-evidence-kernel.yaml; contracts/01-application-attempt-lifecycle.yaml; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§4.2 and 5.3."
x-ownership: consumer: owns: [task_intent, task_permissions, selected_subject, declared_assistance, admission_decision] restriction: >- Selection and permission do not establish capability satisfaction or application commitment. Authentication comes from the channel, not a caller-supplied principal/provenance field. connector: owns: [preparation, local_handle, dispatch_observations, observation_window, translation, local_control_evidence] restriction: >- Publishes dispatch and observation only under the commission's grants. It may faithfully publish subject claims as the designated execution writer, but does not become their semantic author. subject: owns: [native_execution_claims, native_capability_declarations] restriction: "Declarations and claims are not independent assessments." origin: owns: [application_facts] restriction: >- Browser-visible receipts collected by a connector remain observations until the separately authorized origin-fact recorder verifies their source, meaning, and correlation. consumer_assessor: owns: [requirement_assessment, reconciliation, diagnostic] restriction: >- Hellscape assesses practice execution; job-hunter's authorized reconciler assesses production evidence. Neither edits source claims or origin facts. x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part VI; contracts/01-application-attempt-lifecycle.yaml."
x-operations: Describe: request: "#/$defs/DescribeRequest" result: "#/$defs/ConnectorDescriptor" semantics: >- Return the configured subject/version, complete capability declaration, native mappings, and configured limits. Do not run a task, probe speculative endpoints, start a browser, or certify the subject. x-status: extracted x-source: *d Prepare: request: "#/$defs/PrepareRequest" result: "#/$defs/PrepareResult" semantics: >- Validate the admitted scope and task, disclose assistance and mapping limitations, serialize the intended native request, and persist immutable preparation. No target browsing, task execution, hidden planning, context reset, or recovery occurs. x-status: inferred x-source: *d Start: request: "#/$defs/StartRequest" result: "#/$defs/StartResult" semantics: >- Durably allocate or recover a local handle and enqueue one logical execution. Return without waiting for native completion. A separately authorized same-key resume is not a second logical execution. x-status: inferred x-source: "3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§5.2–5.3 and 10.6; 4-circus-tent-arch.md §5.6." Observe: request: "#/$defs/ObserveRequest" result: "#/$defs/ObservationPage" semantics: >- Read accumulated, journal-backed observations through an explicit prefix. Bounded waiting and pagination do not imply a native polling endpoint. Observation remains available for late evidence after local closure. x-status: inferred x-source: *d RequestNativeCancel: request: "#/$defs/NativeCancelRequest" result: "#/$defs/ControlReceipt" semantics: >- Invoke only a mapped native cancellation operation, or report unsupported mapping/unknown delivery honestly. Preserve request, acknowledgement, subject stop claim, independently observed effect, and timing separately. x-status: inferred x-source: *d CloseObservationConnection: request: "#/$defs/CloseConnectionRequest" result: "#/$defs/ControlReceipt" semantics: >- Close the connector-owned native observation transport. The explicit end_observation flag additionally requests bounded local finalization, never native cancellation. Neither action establishes no-commit. x-status: proposed x-source: *w CollectArtifacts: request: "#/$defs/CollectArtifactsRequest" result: - "#/$defs/ArtifactInventory" - "#/$defs/ArtifactChunk" semantics: >- Enumerate or transfer retained artifacts, optionally retrieving already produced artifacts through an evidenced native retrieval contract. Return explicit missingness. Never rerun a task to manufacture an artifact. x-status: inferred x-source: *d ReleaseNativeContext: request: "#/$defs/ReleaseContextRequest" result: "#/$defs/ControlReceipt" semantics: >- Use a mapped native release operation for the specified context, or report unsupported. Do not silently log out, purge a profile, terminate unrelated work, or substitute process containment. x-status: inferred x-source: "3-hellscape-blueprint.md §5; 4-circus-tent-arch.md §5.3." Contain: request: "#/$defs/ContainRequest" result: "#/$defs/ControlReceipt" semantics: >- Execute an independently authorized, versioned harness policy against a bounded resource scope. No arbitrary shell command is accepted. Record known affected attempts and unresolved impact. x-status: inferred x-source: "3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§5.5 and 13."
x-reference-carrier: classification: provisional profile: connector-http-json/0.1.0 method: POST path: /connector base_address: deployment_configured_no_default_host_or_port media_type: application/json encoding: UTF-8 behavior: - >- Each call carries one ConnectorRequest and returns one ConnectorResponse. Start is asynchronous with respect to task execution; Observe uses bounded pull pages. No WebSocket, SSE, or native GET-runs endpoint is required. - >- A normal result uses HTTP 200. Typed connector errors use an appropriate 4xx/5xx transport status; clients inspect the typed body, not status alone. A valid observed native failure remains a normal Observe result. - >- Undecodable or unauthenticated traffic may be rejected before a correlated ConnectorResponse can be constructed. Such a transport rejection conveys no task outcome and must not reveal another principal's handles. - >- Authenticate and authorize the channel independently of request IDs. Use an authenticated local channel or TLS-protected deployment channel; credentials are configured outside these JSON records. reason: >- A single small JSON carrier permits independently implemented Python, Rust, Go, and language-undecided consumers without coupling to a native REST API. Pull observations avoid requiring native callbacks or streaming support. flip_condition: >- Add a separately versioned carrier if measured deployment requirements need streaming, another authenticated IPC mechanism, or different transfer efficiency. Preserve the nine verbs, messages, ownership, and evidence rules. x-status: proposed x-source: *w
x-hashing: profile: kernel-jcs-sha256/1 rules: artifact: SHA-256_of_exact_stored_bytes structured_record: SHA-256_of_RFC8785_canonical_complete_record native_request_hash: SHA-256_of_exact_retained_native_request_bytes delivered_task_hash: SHA-256_of_exact_retained_subject_facing_task_bytes task_semantic_hash: >- SHA-256 of the canonical TaskEnvelope after removing task_id and replacing entry.url with entry.logical_id and each permitted_origins entry's origin with that entry's logical_id. All other values and array order remain. semantic_profile: external-connector-task/1 constraints: - >- Logical entry/origin IDs are immutable, unique within their scope, and bound to actual destinations by the admitted manifest. A semantic hash is a comparison key, not permission to change a destination. - >- The full task digest, actual destinations, complete preparation, subject identity, permissions, and native request digest are pinned separately. An equal semantic hash cannot bypass changed-input or commissioning checks. - >- Runtime credentials and signing values are not task semantics. Store secret material through scoped runtime access bindings, not ordinary task fields or logs.
