These are capability declarations, not shared browser primitives or compulsory success gates. x-status: proposed x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part VI; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§2.1, 4.3, and 5.1."
x-invariants: - id: EXT-SURFACE classification: invariant rule: >- Recognize exactly the nine versioned verbs. The shared request surface is task-shaped and browser-agnostic. No shared Page, ElementHandle, selector engine, DOM node handle, or synchronous browser primitive is defined here. Native input formats are mapping artifacts, not a cross-browser API. derivation: "Unifying browser primitives repeats the Stagehand-on-Juggler failure." x-status: extracted x-source: *b
- id: EXT-AUTHORITY classification: invariant rule: >- Derive caller identity and grants from authenticated channel registration. Authorize verb, connector, subject, task scope, account/runtime access, artifacts, and control target. IDs and digests are not bearer authority. Application credentials do not grant connector control access. consequence: >- Requests cannot assign server provenance or write origin/report domains. Observation provenance is copied from authenticated kernel ingestion. Hash-valid content from an unauthorized source remains unauthorized. derivation: "HTTP 200, a matching trace, and authentication are different facts." x-status: inferred x-source: "3-hellscape-blueprint.md §3.3; 4-circus-tent-arch.md §5.8; 5-browser-qualification.md."
- id: EXT-DESCRIBE classification: invariant rule: >- Pin a descriptor to one subject/version/configured mode/interface surface. A new subject version starts unknown on every capability until its own evidence establishes another availability. Neither presence nor absence inherits. Documentation can support a declaration, not a run-success result. consequence: >- Complete operation-handler coverage does not mean complete native mapping. An unmapped operation is not automatically native absence. A watchdog, fixture namespace, or forced termination cannot establish a native capability. derivation: "The invalid isolation control and version-inheritance trap prohibit assumed findings." x-status: extracted x-source: *h
- id: EXT-DECLARE-NOT-ASSESS classification: invariant rule: >- The connector declares capabilities, mappings, observations, and source claims. It does not emit qualification, requirement satisfaction, or an authoritative application-success flag. Consumer assessment remains separate from capability availability and opportunity. derivation: "The judged component must not certify its own behavior." x-status: extracted x-source: *h
- id: EXT-TASK classification: invariant rule: >- Match the full task, scope, permissions, observation policy, assistance, and selected subject to the admitted manifest. Application work additionally matches its immutable commission, including kind and lineage. Manual commissions are not dispatchable through this contract. consequence: >- Laboratory forms remain practice/held_in even with real job content. Discovery and extraction have no fabricated application attempt. Rehearsal completion never authorizes production dispatch. derivation: "Practice facts cannot become production evidence through a connector." x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Parts III and VI; contracts/01-application-attempt-lifecycle.yaml."
- id: EXT-READ-ONLY classification: invariant rule: >- discover_jobs and extract tasks cannot execute employer/application mutations. HTTP method alone does not determine whether an operation is read-only. The crawler cannot gain application authority through an extraction extension, plan artifact, redirect, or permissive task text. consequence: >- Persisting discovery evidence is permitted. An apply/self-referral/contact reveal mutation requires a separately commissioned application task and an authorized executor, not a crawler's write-action stub. derivation: "Stage1's Oregon self-referral example demonstrates the acquisition/mutation boundary." x-status: extracted x-source: *c
- id: EXT-PREPARE classification: invariant rule: >- Prepare is non-executing. Validate already supplied task data, plan, dependencies, mappings, grants, and declared limits without visiting the target, testing authentication, resetting context, invoking a planner, or secretly improving the plan. Record the native serialization and subject-facing task independently. consequence: >- External planning occurs before Prepare with public-observation evidence and disclosed cost. A native goal planner starts only as part of Start. Translation preserves intent, action order, values, targets, and retry policy; it adds no hidden sleeps, selector alternatives, or recovery. Incomplete translation produces UNSUPPORTED_MAPPING. derivation: "Undisclosed assistance makes executor comparisons and attribution meaningless." x-status: inferred x-source: "3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§5.2–5.4."
- id: EXT-PREPARATION-PIN classification: invariant rule: >- A preparation is immutable and names the exact descriptor, subject, mapping, full task, delivered task, intended native request, runtime-access references, and limitations. Start accepts that preparation digest, including all concerns requiring acceptance, under actual task authority. consequence: >- Reject a stale subject/configuration/mapping or changed artifact rather than silently repreparing. A blocking concern never produces a startable preparation. Missing native cancellation alone is not a universal preparation blocker. derivation: "A request audited at preparation must be the request actually dispatched." x-status: inferred x-source: "3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§5 and 10.6; contracts/01-application-attempt-lifecycle.yaml."
- id: EXT-START classification: invariant rule: >- Before wire delivery, durably commit the local handle, immutable request binding, idempotency association, and dispatch intent under owner-local fencing. Start returns a local receipt without awaiting task completion. A native run ID is attached only in later source-backed observations. consequence: >- Local admission, queueing, native acceptance, native execution claims, and origin commitment remain distinct. A crash around delivery yields uncertain unless stronger evidence establishes acceptance or non-acceptance. derivation: "Remote work cannot be atomically committed with a local acknowledgement." x-status: inferred x-source: "3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§5.3 and 10.6; contracts/01-application-attempt-lifecycle.yaml."
- id: EXT-IDEMPOTENCY classification: invariant rule: >- For mutating/collecting calls, (authenticated principal, connector_id, request_id) identifies one command. Same command and identical request returns its retained receipt without another effect; conflicting content under that key is rejected. Describe and Observe are read calls whose responses may reflect newer evidence. consequence: >- Independently index logical execution by (principal, connector_id, Start.idempotency_key), bound to the immutable preparation and commission. Repeated initial Start, even with a new request_id, returns the same handle. An application commission cannot acquire a second logical execution by changing keys, callers, or executors. derivation: "Transport retries must not create repeated applications." x-status: inferred x-source: "4-circus-tent-arch.md §5.6; contracts/01-application-attempt-lifecycle.yaml LIFE-IDEMPOTENCY."
- id: EXT-RESUME classification: invariant rule: >- Resume requires a new command identity, the existing logical idempotency key/handle, explicit recovery authority, and an evidenced native checkpoint or idempotency contract for the same request and context. It preserves the same logical dispatch and journals each additional delivery. consequence: >- Never repeat completed side-effecting steps. Do not resume after the observation window is draining/closed, after context identity changed, or merely because a local lease expired. Unsupported recovery retains uncertainty; a new attempt needs the lifecycle's duplicate-risk review. derivation: "A local checkpoint or lease is not proof that an employer write did not commit." x-status: inferred x-source: "4-circus-tent-arch.md §5.6; contracts/01-application-attempt-lifecycle.yaml."
- id: EXT-OBSERVE classification: proposed_mechanism rule: >- Observe returns registered connector observation projections in journal order for exactly the requested handle. The cursor identifies a scanned journal position, including positions containing other event kinds. It does not claim every journal entry is a connector observation. consequence: >- The first page pins through; continuation pages use that same cutoff. after < entry.sequence <= next <= through. next names the last scanned position, not merely the last returned item. has_more is exactly next.sequence < through.last_sequence. At the cutoff an empty page is legitimate and does not imply native termination or absence of future callbacks. Lost/unavailable cursor history is explicit, never skipped. rationale: "Bounded resumable pulls work even when the native interface has no polling API." flip_condition: >- Introduce another versioned observation carrier if measured workloads need push delivery; retain journal cutoffs, loss visibility, deduplication, ordering, and late-evidence semantics. x-status: proposed x-source: *w
- id: EXT-NORMALIZE classification: invariant rule: >- Retain exact native bodies before normalization. Authenticate source and correlate to the attempt independently. Mismatched/unknown correlation or unverified source yields no accepted execution claims. Trace mismatch may coexist with independently evidenced alternate correlation. consequence: >- Preserve source scope, mapping version, source/receipt times, explicit unknown, missing fields, and conflicting responses/callbacks. None and acknowledgements do not become semantic success. Initially map audited circus-tent /run completed to execution completion only. derivation: "Adapter overclaims are connector defects, not native subject claims." x-status: extracted x-source: *d
- id: EXT-CLOSE classification: invariant rule: >- Closing a connection, ending observation, requesting native cancellation, releasing context, and containment are separate operations/effects. end_observation=true stops new workflow commands and starts the commissioned bounded drain/finalization; false closes only the selected native transport. Neither setting implies a cancel request. consequence: >- Local deadlines remain effective without native cancellation. Freeze close-time knowledge and pins; append late evidence and new owner/report revisions without reopening the window or rewriting the original snapshot. Only a fixture origin can seal its mutation authority. derivation: "Post-disconnect continuation is the paid-for cancellation counterexample." x-status: inferred x-source: "3-hellscape-blueprint.md §5.5; contracts/01-application-attempt-lifecycle.yaml."
- id: EXT-CONTROLS classification: invariant rule: >- Every control operation has a scoped authorization and immutable observations. requested records a request attempt, acknowledged records a verified response, and effect_observed requires effect evidence. A subject's confirmed-stop report is still a subject claim. consequence: >- Unknown delivery is not unsupported and unsupported mapping is not automatically native absence. Release failure cannot silently trigger Contain. Forced termination is not cooperative cancellation or rollback. Cleanup of shared resources must identify known affected attempts. derivation: "An acknowledgement does not establish the requested semantic effect." x-status: inferred x-source: "3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§4.1 and 5.5; 5-browser-qualification.md."
- id: EXT-BOUNDS classification: invariant rule: >- Enforce finite local call, queue/observation, drain, cancellation-wait, and cleanup-wait bounds using registered local monotonic clocks. Admission and observation buffering are bounded; rejected work is not silently lost. An accepted queued task consumes its active observation budget. consequence: >- No workflow delivery starts after its active boundary. A call deadline does not stop native work already dispatched. Record budget enforcement ownership and gaps; Start cannot silently downgrade a required bound or requested state policy. A zero configured bound means immediate, not absent. Reserve progress for local close/control handling despite task queue pressure. derivation: "A stuck native call must not prevent the observer from truthfully finalizing." x-status: inferred x-source: "3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§5.5 and 10.6; 2-state-bank-crawler-blueprint.json Decision 2."
- id: EXT-STATE-POLICY classification: invariant rule: >- Browser-state and framework-learning-state requests remain separate. Prepare records their mapping and limitations; actual realization is journaled after Start. An opaque context reference is not a Page or DOM handle and grants no authority by itself. consequence: >- Do not call a subject-default context fresh, infer isolation from a fixture namespace, or claim clean learning state from a fresh browser profile. Required unsupported policies reject preparation; explicitly permitted best-effort policies disclose their limitations before Start. derivation: "Fixture, browser, and learning state have different contamination boundaries." x-status: inferred x-source: "3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§3.4 and 5.1."
- id: EXT-ARTIFACTS classification: invariant rule: >- Install immutable artifact bytes durably before journal references. Artifact names and digests resolve only within the authorized handle's retained evidence or declared native retrieval mapping. Do not fetch arbitrary caller URLs or filesystem paths through CollectArtifacts. consequence: >- Each requested name receives an available slot or reasoned missingness; known digests survive loss. Inventory completeness concerns the declared inventory scope, not proof of all private native artifacts. Retrieval never reruns workflow actions, creates a new browser session, or claims a native artifact API exists because local response bytes were captured. derivation: "Evidence references must identify available bytes, not plausible locators." x-status: inferred x-source: "contracts/00-evidence-kernel.yaml EK-ARTIFACTS; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§1.3 and 10."
- id: EXT-EVIDENCE classification: invariant rule: >- ObservationItem copies an already journaled, registry-validated projection. Its metadata must match the referenced event. Nested claims, control observations, and artifact slots cite earlier supporting events, not themselves. Register/import source evidence before citing it. consequence: >- Publish lifecycle domains asynchronously under their own grants. This connector may emit references for dispatch, observation, and faithfully delegated execution publications only. It cannot publish application or report as if those were connector-owned outcomes. derivation: "Unjournaled or self-authenticated data cannot support reproducible assessment." x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part VI; contracts/00-evidence-kernel.yaml; contracts/01-application-attempt-lifecycle.yaml."
- id: EXT-TIME-NULL classification: invariant rule: >- Every normalized null uses Missing with one of the six kernel reasons. Every measurement has clock_id, boot_id, origin, estimate, and censoring. Register clocks before use. Never subtract across clocks or boots; UTC is annotation only. Endpoint differences and bounds obey kernel arithmetic. consequence: >- Preserve reported zero unchanged under its source clock. Missing native timing is unavailable, not zero. Do not divide aggregate latency into step timings or compare unlike intervals as a measurement discrepancy. Configuration limits are declarations, not observed measurements. derivation: "The diagnosed _elapsed() zero defect makes default timing values unsafe." x-status: extracted x-source: *h
- id: EXT-FAILURE classification: invariant rule: >- ConnectorError describes failure to carry out this connector operation, not a composite task outcome. An observed native failed/completed/stopped claim is normal evidence returned by Observe. Local prerequisite and translation errors are not fabricated subject failures. consequence: >- A lost response or storage failure cannot justify a success default, fresh idempotency key, speculative native probe, or silent external retry. Offline evidence replay invokes none of the task/control effects here. derivation: "The retired qualification harness distinguished harness failure from driver behavior." x-status: inferred x-source: "5-browser-qualification.md; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§10.6–10.8."

ObservationPage: type: object additionalProperties: false required: [kind, handle, after, through, next, has_more, observation_close_ref, items, limitations] properties: kind: {const: observation_page, x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} handle: {$ref: "#/$defs/HandleReference", x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} after: {$ref: "#/$defs/ObservationCursor", x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} through: {$ref: "#/$defs/JournalPrefix", x-status: extracted, x-source: *k} next: {$ref: "#/$defs/ObservationCursor", x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} has_more: {type: boolean, x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} observation_close_ref: $ref: "#/$defs/MaybeEvidenceRef" description: Locally observed closure at this cutoff, or not_observed; not native termination. x-status: proposed x-source: *w items: type: array items: {$ref: "#/$defs/ObservationItem"} x-status: proposed x-source: *w limitations: type: array items: {type: string, minLength: 1} x-status: inferred x-source: *d description: >- Entries are unique and increasing by journal sequence. ArtifactChunk: type: object additionalProperties: false required: [kind, handle, digest, size_bytes, offset, returned_bytes, data_base64, chunk_digest, end_of_artifact, evidence_refs] properties: kind: {const: artifact_chunk, x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} handle: {$ref: "#/$defs/HandleReference", x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} digest: {$ref: "#/$defs/Digest", x-status: extracted, x-source: *k} size_bytes: {$ref: "#/$defs/Revision", x-status: extracted, x-source: *k} offset: {$ref: "#/$defs/Revision", x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} returned_bytes: {$ref: "#/$defs/Revision", x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} data_base64: type: string pattern: '^(?:[A-Za-z0-9+/]{4})*(?:[A-Za-z0-9+/]{2}==|[A-Za-z0-9+/]{3}=)?$' x-status: proposed x-source: *w chunk_digest: {$ref: "#/$defs/Digest", x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} end_of_artifact: {type: boolean, x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} evidence_refs: {$ref: "#/$defs/SupportRefs", x-status: inferred, x-source: *k} description: >- Decode canonical padded base64 and verify returned_bytes and chunk_digest. offset equals the request offset; returned_bytes is bounded by request and descriptor limits; offset+returned_bytes <= size_bytes. end_of_artifact is true exactly at size_bytes. Transfer does not change access classification or evidence provenance. x-status: proposed x-source: *w

does not state whether the application committed. x-status: proposed x-source: *w retry_guidance: enum: [same_command_only, new_command_if_not_dispatched, operator_review, do_not_retry] x-status: proposed x-source: *w retry_after: oneOf: - $ref: "#/$defs/DurationLimit" - $ref: "#/$defs/Missing" description: Advisory backoff declaration, not a measured duration or permission to resend native work. x-status: proposed x-source: *w handle: oneOf: - $ref: "#/$defs/HandleReference" - $ref: "#/$defs/Missing" x-status: proposed x-source: *w evidence_refs: {$ref: "#/$defs/EvidenceRefs", x-status: inferred, x-source: *k} allOf: - if: {properties: {code: {const: DELIVERY_UNCERTAIN}}} then: properties: operation_delivery: {const: may_have_dispatched} retry_guidance: {enum: [same_command_only, operator_review, do_not_retry]} - if: {properties: {retry_guidance: {const: new_command_if_not_dispatched}}} then: properties: {operation_delivery: {enum: [not_dispatched, not_applicable]}} description: >- Sanitize details. Retrying the connector command does not authorize a new logical/native execution. x-status: proposed x-source: *w

never an authenticated principal. x-status: proposed x-source: *w connector_id: {$ref: "#/$defs/Identifier", x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} operation: {$ref: "#/$defs/Operation", x-status: extracted, x-source: *h} call_limit: {$ref: "#/$defs/DurationLimit", x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} payload: {type: object, x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} allOf: - if: {properties: {operation: {const: Describe}}} then: {properties: {payload: {$ref: "#/$defs/DescribeRequest"}}} - if: {properties: {operation: {const: Prepare}}} then: {properties: {payload: {$ref: "#/$defs/PrepareRequest"}}} - if: {properties: {operation: {const: Start}}} then: {properties: {payload: {$ref: "#/$defs/StartRequest"}}} - if: {properties: {operation: {const: Observe}}} then: {properties: {payload: {$ref: "#/$defs/ObserveRequest"}}} - if: {properties: {operation: {const: RequestNativeCancel}}} then: {properties: {payload: {$ref: "#/$defs/NativeCancelRequest"}}} - if: {properties: {operation: {const: CloseObservationConnection}}} then: {properties: {payload: {$ref: "#/$defs/CloseConnectionRequest"}}} - if: {properties: {operation: {const: CollectArtifacts}}} then: {properties: {payload: {$ref: "#/$defs/CollectArtifactsRequest"}}} - if: {properties: {operation: {const: ReleaseNativeContext}}} then: {properties: {payload: {$ref: "#/$defs/ReleaseContextRequest"}}} - if: {properties: {operation: {const: Contain}}} then: {properties: {payload: {$ref: "#/$defs/ContainRequest"}}} description: >- call_limit starts at local authenticated receipt, is bounded by the descriptor, and is not a caller-clock timestamp or native execution timeout. Request identity conflicts compare the complete canonical request. All referenced handles/configurations must identify connector_id. x-status: proposed x-source: *w

$schema: https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema $id: urn:job-application:contracts:internal-browser-binding:browseroxide:0.1.0 title: BrowserOxide native binding description: >- Review draft of the BrowserOxide-only synchronous primitive contract. This is the first of two independent schema documents in this file. It is not a browser-neutral dispatcher, an external connector, or a selection of Ringmaster's packaging. Native Page, DOM, solver, and V8 objects retain their native ownership and lifetime rules. x-status: proposed x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Parts III, V, VI, and VIII; governing task, Products."
x-source-index: handoff: &h "1-handoff-brief.txt, Parts III, V, VI, and VIII–X" engine: &e "2-state-bank-crawler-blueprint.json, §§3–4, 5.5, 9–10, and Decision 2" acquisition: &a "2-state-bank-crawler-blueprint.json, §§3, 7–8, and 13" diagnostic: &d "3-hellscape-blueprint.md, §§3–5 and 10" qualification: &q "5-browser-qualification.md, Evidence discipline" kernel: &k "contracts/00-evidence-kernel.yaml, evidence-kernel/0.1.0" external: &x "contracts/02-external-connector.yaml, external-connector/0.1.0" task: &t "Governing task, Products: BrowserOxide direct DOM/V8 access and open Ringmaster packaging decision." wire: &w >- Proposed BrowserOxide-only primitive and evidence representations. Operation names and argument/result shapes below are contract proposals, not assertions that these exact Rust methods already exist.
x-contract: name: internal-browser-binding/browseroxide version: 0.1.0 maturity: review_draft owner: contracts implementation_owner: BrowserOxide_binding_maintainer consumers: [crawler, Ringmaster] conformance_suite: conformance/03-internal-browser-binding.md suite_instance: BrowserOxide schema_entrypoints: - "#/$defs/BOBindingDescriptor" - "#/$defs/BOPrimitiveRecord" - "#/$defs/BODomExport" execution_shape: synchronous_native_primitive external_connector_version: external-connector/0.1.0 evidence_kernel_version: evidence-kernel/0.1.0 x-status: proposed x-source: *h
x-boundary: rule: >- BrowserOxide scraping and application execution may share BrowserOxide-native implementation. Neither shares primitives, handles, selector machinery, or implementation with the Camoufox binding. Shared definitions copied here describe evidence, not a cross-browser runtime interface. packaging: >- Ringmaster's in-process/FFI, separate-binary/API, or extension/controller packaging decision remains open for its PRD. Wherever the native operation executes, its Page and isolate stay on their owning OS thread. A process boundary may carry owned data, never a live DOM/V8 pointer. purpose: >- This binding enables discovery and real applications; its construction or qualification must not delay manually recorded production applications. An HTTP-only crawler slice may publish its actual narrower scope without claiming unexercised browser capabilities. x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Parts V and VII–IX; governing task, Products."
x-representation: rule: >- PrimitiveRecord is an audit representation of a typed native call and its return, not a JSON RPC protocol. Same-thread code may use native borrows directly; it is not required to serialize the DOM to call another native operation. BOPageRef, BORootRef, and BONodeRef are diagnostic identities attached to live native objects. Deserializing one never creates a usable native handle or grants permission. validation: >- Parse this YAML document independently of the Camoufox document. Resolve only local schema references. Enforce JSON Schema 2020-12 plus BO rules, date-time formats, reference resolution, authorization, and hash checks. Reject duplicate mapping keys, non-finite numbers, unknown versions, and undeclared fields. Raw null is accepted only inside Missing.value. timing: >- A binding's own elapsed timer is subject_reported evidence, even if measured accurately with a monotonic clock. Browser-origin measurements are separately browser_measured. The consumer's independent engine_measured timing is not replaced by either. Configuration limits are not measurements. x-status: proposed x-source: "contracts/00-evidence-kernel.yaml; 2-state-bank-crawler-blueprint.json §5.5."
x-source-reconciliation: - decision: >- The supplied crawler blueprint already specifies Rust/BrowserOxide transport, thread, and session behavior. Those detailed constraints are retained; no Camoufox crawler assumption is imported into this binding. x-status: extracted x-source: *e - decision: >- Page::from_html, Page::challenge_verdict, reset_for_reuse, navigate_with_init(client), HttpClient::shared(profile), and ordinary HttpClient::clone are documentary native anchors. Their complete Rust signatures and current implementation inventory are not supplied. The proposed primitives below require explicit versioned native mappings. x-status: inferred x-source: *e - decision: >- HTTP acquisition remains a first-class BrowserOxide facility. Page is not treated as an operational superset: incomplete browser rendering may coexist with a complete response from the correctly retained live client. x-status: extracted x-source: "2-state-bank-crawler-blueprint.json §§3.2 and 3.6." - decision: >- No supplied source establishes current screenshot, file-assignment, closed-root, trusted-input, or native-interruption support for a particular BrowserOxide build. Naming a primitive reserves a contract, not a present capability. x-status: uncertain x-source: "The current BrowserOxide source/API inventory and executed binding evidence are absent." - decision: >- No handoff amendment is introduced. Browser-specific catalog and audit encodings are proposed mechanisms; no new native capability is assumed. x-status: proposed x-source: *w
x-native-catalog: required_capability_ids: - bo.direct_dom - bo.direct_v8 - bo.live_http_client - bo.http_pool_sharing - bo.offline_from_html - bo.frame_dom - bo.open_shadow_dom - bo.closed_shadow_dom - bo.dom_value_mutation - bo.composed_event_dispatch - bo.file_assignment - bo.raster_capture - bo.reset_dom_invalidation - bo.native_deadline_interruption rule: >- These IDs form the minimum BrowserOxide catalog. Each appears exactly once in the pinned capability catalog and descriptor, including unknown entries. Additional capabilities require an explicitly versioned catalog. New primitives require a BrowserOxide schema revision, not a matching Camoufox operation or a browser-neutral escape hatch. flip_condition: >- Refine this proposed inventory when the pinned engine API and native conformance fixtures establish better primitive boundaries. Preserve direct access, native ownership, and truthful unsupported results. x-status: proposed x-source: *w
x-rules: - id: BO-NATIVE classification: invariant rule: >- Mapped operations enter BrowserOxide's native API directly. DOM and V8 operations must not route through CDP, Playwright, Juggler, another browser, or a shared browser adapter. Reading serialized HTML through a bridge is not evidence of direct native DOM access. derivation: >- The Stagehand-on-Juggler failure shows why a lowest-common-denominator internal abstraction removes the capabilities the framework needs. x-status: extracted x-source: *h
- id: BO-THREAD classification: invariant rule: >- Allocate, enter, reset, and destroy a Page on its owning OS thread. Page, isolate-local values, DOM borrows, solver instances, and closures capturing them never cross that thread boundary. A call is synchronous: it returns a value or a typed failure, not a task handle for later polling. consequence: >- Queues and durable I/O may yield outside native execution. Cross-thread messages contain owned bytes, immutable descriptions, IDs, and only those live HTTP-client handles whose Send/sharing semantics are established. Reject wrong-thread use before entering the engine. derivation: "The supplied Page contract is stricter than merely locking a V8 isolate." x-status: extracted x-source: *e
- id: BO-HTTP classification: invariant rule: >- Preserve live-client identity, pool identity, profile, session domain, epoch, request order, and cookie-application order. An ordinary client clone has an independent pool; it is not a shared-pool handle. Stateful and rotating sessions admit at most one request affecting a jar until redirects and cookie updates have completed. consequence: >- With a process-global SharedSession, independent session domains use separate engine processes unless namespacing is independently verified. A persisted cookie snapshot is recovery evidence, not permission to distribute a rotating session or resume it after an owner crash. derivation: "Concurrent Set-Cookie application and accidental process-global sharing break session continuity." x-status: extracted x-source: *e
- id: BO-OFFLINE classification: invariant rule: >- bo.from_html performs no network acquisition. Its inputs and required rendering resources must already be available. If required resources are absent, report an unmet precondition; the acquisition controller may then choose a separately evidenced cold navigation. consequence: >- Preserve each transport attempt and verdict. Neither successful bootstrap nor challenge clearance alone establishes accepted job content. Structured JSON must be validated and normalized before an HTML-only render classifier receives it. derivation: "The hybrid acquisition contract cannot be reproduced if from_html secretly fetches." x-status: extracted x-source: *a
- id: BO-DOM classification: invariant rule: >- Native DOM observations retain frame, document, root, and node identity. Navigation, replacement, reset, and destruction invalidate affected identities before reuse. Removed/replaced nodes cannot be resurrected by reusing an ID. Reject stale references before mutation. consequence: >- Report inaccessible frames, closed roots, truncation, and observation gaps explicitly. Missing access is not an empty complete tree. Direct DOM access does not by itself establish closed-root access, rendering fidelity, trusted input, isolation, or origin compatibility. derivation: "Observation coverage and native access are different properties." x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Parts III and VI; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§2.1 and 4."
- id: BO-INPUT classification: invariant rule: >- Direct property mutation, synthetic DOM event dispatch, and native browser input are different mechanisms. This catalog exposes property mutation and event dispatch explicitly; it does not label either as trusted user input. Preserve bubbles, cancelable, and composed settings and actual event observations. consequence: >- A returned native call, None/unit return, setter readback, or dispatched click event is not application acceptance or commitment. No hidden selector healing, planner, retry loop, alternate browser, or direct employer API submission may be added by the binding. derivation: "Acknowledgement is not semantic success; undisclosed assistance corrupts attribution." x-status: inferred x-source: "5-browser-qualification.md; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§4.6 and 5.4."
- id: BO-AUTHORITY classification: invariant rule: >- Every call is bound to an admitted task/resource grant. Artifact references, scripts, node IDs, and URLs do not grant authority. Crawler acquisition and extraction cannot invoke application mutations through DOM writes, V8 evaluation, redirects, or a query POST with hidden write semantics. consequence: >- bo.http_exchange is acquisition-only. Application interaction requires the separately commissioned executor scope. Script evaluation obeys the same target, data, and effect permissions as other primitives. derivation: "The crawler's write-action stub and Oregon self-referral counterexample prohibit acquisition-to-apply escalation." x-status: extracted x-source: *a
- id: BO-REUSE classification: invariant rule: >- reset_for_reuse clears the native DOM registry and invalidates old DOM references while preserving the intended cookie jar. Increment the page generation before making a reset Page available again. Reuse is confined to compatible process, profile, target, and session-generation scope. consequence: >- A failed reset quarantines the Page for owner-thread destruction. Bootstrap remains cold. No retained Page or solver moves to a replacement worker, and no pool reset proves browser-state isolation. derivation: "Warmth must not retain stale native objects or cross session ownership." x-status: extracted x-source: "2-state-bank-crawler-blueprint.json §§9.6 and 10."
- id: BO-TIME classification: invariant rule: >- Every measurement identifies origin, clock_id, and boot_id and uses exact, bounded, or unavailable estimation with censoring. Endpoint subtraction requires one registered clock/boot/origin and ordered endpoints. Zero is valid. UTC is annotation only. consequence: >- A local waiting deadline is not a native timeout or proof of interruption. If a synchronous engine call cannot be interrupted, the supervisor may contain its owner separately; the binding records uncertainty rather than inventing native cancellation. Do not compare offsets across restarts. derivation: "The _elapsed() defect and the qualification timeout distinction forbid default-zero and timeout-as-cancel semantics." x-status: extracted x-source: *h
- id: BO-EVIDENCE classification: invariant rule: >- Journal the evidence needed to reconstruct a call before citing its record. Mutating calls require a durable authorized intent before native entry. Install immutable artifacts before registration. Record native returns and errors without strengthening their semantics. consequence: >- Primitive records are observations or subject claims, never origin facts. The ingestion authority assigns provenance; these records cannot set it. Timings copied into the kernel retain their original origin. Secrets stay in controlled session storage; sensitive native bytes are restricted artifacts. A record cannot cite its own future registration. derivation: "Unjournaled native observations cannot become retroactive diagnostic evidence." x-status: inferred x-source: "contracts/00-evidence-kernel.yaml; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§3.3 and 10."
- id: BO-CAPS classification: invariant rule: >- Capability evidence is scoped to the exact binding build, engine build, configuration, mode, and interface surface. A new subject version starts unknown. Mapped does not mean exercised; unsupported mapping does not establish native absence. Capability, opportunity, and result remain separate in the consumer's diagnostic. consequence: >- The BrowserOxide suite must prove actual direct DOM/V8 access for a full-strength binding claim; that test cannot be exempted away. A narrower HTTP-only release must identify unexercised browser capabilities. Passing a binding fixture does not qualify an employer origin. derivation: "No inheritance and held-in/held-out separation prevent untested capability promotion." x-status: extracted x-source: *h
x-open-evidence: - missing: Current BrowserOxide API inventory, build identity, and native action/capture implementations. resolution: >- Inspect the pinned engine source and compile minimal owner-thread fixtures for direct DOM, V8, frames/roots, event semantics, upload, capture, and interruption. Record exact native symbols and executed evidence separately. Until then, descriptors must not advertise these as demonstrated. x-status: uncertain x-source: "2-state-bank-crawler-blueprint.json references an engine inventory but does not supply it." - missing: Engine-level namespacing of process-global session storage. resolution: >- Run same-origin controlled write/read and rotating-cookie tests with valid controls. Until established, preserve the source's separate-process allocation for independent session domains. x-status: uncertain x-source: "2-state-bank-crawler-blueprint.json Decision 2 and §9."

--- $schema: https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema $id: urn:job-application:contracts:internal-browser-binding:camoufox:0.1.0 title: Camoufox Firefox-native binding description: >- Review draft of the Camoufox-only synchronous primitive contract for the Python Circus Tent implementation. This independent schema is not a variant of the BrowserOxide primitive schema. It distinguishes a proposed in-browser Firefox extension surface from the documented Playwright-to-Juggler compatibility path without claiming the extension has been built. x-status: proposed x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Parts III, V, VI, and VIII; governing task, Products."
x-source-index: handoff: &h "1-handoff-brief.txt, Parts III, V, VI, and VIII–X" native: &n "4-circus-tent-arch.md, §§2–5 and 6" diagnostic: &d "3-hellscape-blueprint.md, §§3–5 and 10" qualification: &q "5-browser-qualification.md, Evidence discipline" kernel: &k "contracts/00-evidence-kernel.yaml, evidence-kernel/0.1.0" external: &x "contracts/02-external-connector.yaml, external-connector/0.1.0" task: &t "Governing task, Products: Circus Tent's current bridge stack and ideal Firefox-extension/controller pattern." wire: &w >- Proposed Camoufox-only primitive, extension-surface, and transcript design. fx operation names and token shapes are not claims about existing Firefox, Juggler, Playwright, or Camoufox methods.
x-contract: name: internal-browser-binding/camoufox version: 0.1.0 maturity: review_draft owner: contracts implementation_owner: Camoufox_binding_maintainer consumers: [Circus Tent] controller_language: Python conformance_suite: conformance/03-internal-browser-binding.md suite_instance: Camoufox schema_entrypoints: - "#/$defs/CFBindingDescriptor" - "#/$defs/CFPrimitiveTranscript" - "#/$defs/CFReduction" execution_shape: synchronous_firefox_primitive external_connector_version: external-connector/0.1.0 evidence_kernel_version: evidence-kernel/0.1.0 x-status: proposed x-source: *h
x-boundary: rule: >- Circus Tent and Ringmaster share the external connector and evidence discipline, not an internal driver API. No conversion between CFTargetRef and a BrowserOxide DOM reference exists. The Python controller owns learn-run-heal, selector tiers, extraction policy, and application planning; the native binding performs only explicitly requested primitives. target_architecture: >- A Firefox extension exposes a richer browser-resident observation/action surface to Python, bypassing Playwright and Juggler for page operations. Its protocol, permissions, and actual API coverage must be established for a pinned implementation. This is the proposed native path, not an assertion of current capability or a transplanted Chromium ModCDP implementation. compatibility_scope: >- The documented Python-to-Playwright-to-Juggler-to-Camoufox path remains identifiable for maintenance and honest execution evidence. Passing its compatibility cases does not certify extension bypass or full-strength native-surface access. A compatibility route cannot silently become the fallback beneath an extension-native claim. x-status: inferred x-source: "Governing task, Products; 1-handoff-brief.txt Parts III and V."
x-representation: rule: >- The schema describes synchronous Python-facing primitive calls and their retained transcripts. An extension may transport request/reply messages internally, and the existing driver may await its protocol internally. Neither exposes a task handle or a shared browser abstraction to its caller. Each call returns a native observation or an explicit bounded uncertainty. tokens: >- CFTabRef, CFDocumentRef, and CFTargetRef identify Firefox browsing contexts, document lifetimes, and binding-local target registrations. They are not Playwright ElementHandle objects, transferable DOM objects, durable selectors, or bearer capabilities. Only the matching native binding can resolve a live token. validation: >- Validate this document independently using JSON Schema 2020-12 and all CF rules. All schema references are local. Reject duplicate mapping keys, non-finite numbers, unknown versions, unknown fields, and bare normalized nulls. Enforce date-time/URI formats and kernel evidence/hash semantics. x-status: proposed x-source: *w
x-source-reconciliation: - decision: >- The architecture's async Playwright implementation is historical implementation guidance, not permission to define an async task-shaped internal binding. The handoff's synchronous primitive boundary wins; awaiting a Firefox-specific transport internally does not change it. x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part VI; 4-circus-tent-arch.md §§3–5." - decision: >- Browser-resident DOM reduction, semantic attributes, explicit open-root traversal, frame accounting, localized capture, and profile-safe recycling survive the architectural revision. Their implementation is Firefox-specific. x-status: extracted x-source: *n - decision: >- The documented page.evaluate, page.frames, page.set_input_files, and DataTransfer-based upload paths are compatibility mapping evidence only. They do not establish an extension API, closed-root access, native input trust, or performance for a new version. x-status: inferred x-source: "4-circus-tent-arch.md §§5.4–5.6; governing task, Products." - decision: >- Network-idle and DOM-quiet heuristics are not universal readiness or application-success predicates. The binding exposes an explicit scoped wait; task-specific readiness and validation semantics belong above it. x-status: inferred x-source: "3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§6.3 and 9.2 overrides universal interpretation of 4-circus-tent-arch.md §5.4." - decision: >- Historical tab caps, recycling thresholds, crop padding, reduction budgets, and model choices are not portfolio constants. Bindings publish actual configured bounds and mappings; the contract specifies their semantics. x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Parts VI–VIII; 4-circus-tent-arch.md §§5–7." - decision: >- No handoff amendment is introduced. The extension direction comes from the governing task; its unresolved implementation is not filled with an invented endpoint, permission grant, or native primitive. x-status: proposed x-source: *t
x-native-catalog: required_capability_ids: - cf.extension_page_surface - cf.page_script_evaluation - cf.frame_observation - cf.open_shadow_observation - cf.closed_shadow_observation - cf.native_input - cf.synthetic_drag_drop - cf.native_file_input - cf.localized_capture - cf.profile_persistence - cf.fingerprint_persistence - cf.browser_context_isolation - cf.native_wait_termination - cf.profile_safe_shutdown rule: >- Enumerate every capability exactly once for this subject/version/mode/route. Unknown is the initial value for a new version. Route and mapping declarations are separate from capability availability and consumer assessment. flip_condition: >- Revise this proposed Camoufox catalog when implemented Firefox-native APIs and their conformance evidence justify a different native cut. Never require a corresponding BrowserOxide operation or hide a capability loss behind a cross-browser facade. x-status: proposed x-source: *w
x-rules: - id: CF-ROUTE classification: invariant rule: >- Pin the actual page-operation route in the binding descriptor and every transcript. For extension_native, all mapped page operations execute through the pinned Firefox extension surface, with no Playwright/Juggler page-operation hop. Profile launch/exit may use a declared native controller lifecycle mapping. consequence: >- Route changes require a new scoped binding/subject configuration and invalidate old tokens. They cannot occur silently inside an already commissioned execution. The legacy route remains labeled compatibility, not a passed extension-bypass claim. derivation: "Otherwise the proposed native surface would conceal the same bridge limitation it exists to remove." x-status: inferred x-source: *t
- id: CF-SYNC classification: invariant rule: >- Each primitive is synchronous at the Python binding boundary. Serialize context-affecting operations within the relevant tab/profile lifetime. Return a value or typed error/uncertainty; do not return a workflow handle or perform undisclosed online planning, healing, retries, or alternate selector actions. consequence: >- A local waiting deadline may end the call without proving that a remote Firefox operation stopped. Mark that uncertainty, fence dependent actions until safe, and leave containment to its separately authorized operation. Do not deadlock the event loop responsible for servicing the reply. derivation: "The external asynchronous task contract and native primitive contract are different boundaries." x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part VI; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §5.5."
- id: CF-PROFILE classification: invariant rule: >- A domain-family profile has one owning browser process at a time. Its fingerprint manifest is immutable. Launch-option or fingerprint changes require an explicit full reset and authentication handoff, not reuse of existing session material under a new identity. consequence: >- Before reuse of a profile directory after shutdown, preserve session state, close the old browser, and obtain actual process-exit/reaping evidence. A close acknowledgement or elapsed grace period is insufficient. Recycling does not rotate fingerprints or copy a live Firefox profile. derivation: "Overlapping Firefox writers risk profile corruption; identity drift invalidates persistent authentication." x-status: extracted x-source: "4-circus-tent-arch.md §§5.2–5.3 and 6."
- id: CF-STATE classification: invariant rule: >- Profile persistence, tab creation, browser-context isolation, and learning state are distinct. A new tab in a persistent profile is not automatically a fresh or isolated browser context. A fresh browser does not erase selector/coordinate caches or framework learning. consequence: >- Bind every document and target token to its tab, document epoch, profile process generation, and binding route. Navigation or node replacement invalidates affected tokens. Reject stale tokens before input; do not silently resolve a different element. derivation: "The historical invalid isolation control cannot establish isolation or leakage." x-status: inferred x-source: "3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§1.3 and 3.4; 4-circus-tent-arch.md §5."
- id: CF-STRUCTURE classification: invariant rule: >- Reduce DOM inside the browser before transferring large page content. Preserve role, aria-label, title, alt, useful text, and meaningful icon semantics under the selected reduction profile. Traverse open roots explicitly; ordinary cloning/query selection does not expose their contents. consequence: >- Keep frame/root boundaries and document epochs in the reduced representation. Readable nested frames contribute scoped content; unreadable frames and roots contribute explicit boundary records/markers. Closed-root access is reported only when the exact configured native route establishes it. Truncation or redaction is visible, never represented as complete absence. derivation: "Flattening without scope and silent omission make later target resolution and diagnosis unsound." x-status: inferred x-source: "4-circus-tent-arch.md §5.4; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§3.3 and 4."
- id: CF-INPUT classification: invariant rule: >- Preserve the requested native-input versus DOM-property/event mechanism. Record actual event semantics where observed. Synthetic DataTransfer drag/drop is labeled synthetic; assigning files is not evidence that the server accepted an upload. None and protocol acknowledgement are not successful form postconditions. consequence: >- Ambiguous target resolution returns all bounded matches; it never silently clicks the first. A side-effecting primitive is not automatically retried after uncertain delivery. A submit click cannot write the application axis. derivation: "The qualification discipline and claim/origin separation prohibit semantic-success inflation." x-status: inferred x-source: "5-browser-qualification.md; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §4.6; 4-circus-tent-arch.md §5.6."
- id: CF-IMAGE classification: invariant rule: >- Capture records the document epoch, requested crop, actual coordinate-space measurements, and image identity. A controller must verify the viewport, scale, frame offset, and layout validity before using coordinates. consequence: >- A perceptual-hash hit alone does not prove that a cached coordinate still identifies the intended control. Crop requests must not silently become full-page captures or use stale geometry. Missing geometry is explicit and cannot be treated as zero offset or unit scale. derivation: "Image similarity is not semantic target identity." x-status: inferred x-source: "4-circus-tent-arch.md §5.6; 5-browser-qualification.md."
- id: CF-TIME classification: invariant rule: >- Use kernel Measurement for every measured interval or scalar. Register independent controller, browser-document, and native-report clocks. Never subtract across clocks or boots. A controller's own reported timer remains subject_reported; it does not become Hellscape's independent clock. consequence: >- Native timeout, local waiting deadline, connection loss, and forced termination remain separate. Preserve exact zero, bounded/censored intervals, and reasoned unavailability. No default zero or invented per-step duration is permitted. derivation: "The diagnosed _elapsed() behavior and cancellation evidence require explicit timing provenance." x-status: extracted x-source: *h
- id: CF-EVIDENCE classification: invariant rule: >- Authorize each primitive against the commissioned task and resource scope. Journal durable intent before potentially side-effecting input. Preserve native replies and errors as immutable evidence before normalization. The ingestion authority, not the controller or extension payload, assigns provenance. consequence: >- Extension telemetry cannot emit origin commitment or verification facts. Scripts and artifact references cannot bypass target, account, upload, or data-destination permissions. Raw secrets/session material are not ordinary journal data. Sensitive DOM, images, and replies use restricted artifacts. A transcript never cites its future registration as support. derivation: "Browser observations are not application authority, and unjournaled evidence cannot support replay." x-status: inferred x-source: "contracts/00-evidence-kernel.yaml; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§3.3 and 10; 4-circus-tent-arch.md §§5.8 and 5.11."
- id: CF-CAPS classification: invariant rule: >- New Camoufox, driver, extension, binding, or materially changed configured subject versions do not inherit capability presence or absence. Map only evidenced native surfaces. A missing extension mapping does not establish that Firefox itself lacks the capability. consequence: >- Run conformance independently for the declared route. Compatibility exemptions cannot certify extension bypass or waive ownership, timing, provenance, missingness, or truthful input semantics. Preserve Firefox, Gecko, NSS, and profile-specific strengths rather than imposing a BrowserOxide-shaped primitive vocabulary. derivation: "The two products remain independent bets; a shared internal abstraction repeats the failed port." x-status: extracted x-source: *h
x-open-evidence: - missing: Firefox-extension transport, permissions, packaging, signing, and current Camoufox support. resolution: >- Inspect the pinned Camoufox/Firefox extension environment. Build a small extension/controller specimen proving browser-resident DOM reduction, target identity, frame/root coverage, input semantics, and page-operation bypass of Playwright/Juggler. Measure rather than assume latency. Do not select an undocumented transport or claim privileged access. x-status: uncertain x-source: *t - missing: Current native upload, closed-root, capture, wait-interruption, and profile-flush behavior for that extension. resolution: >- Exercise local controlled fixtures with independent postconditions and valid controls. Keep each unavailable mapping explicit; continue honest compatibility/manual work without treating these unknowns as a portfolio gate. x-status: uncertain x-source: "Governing task, Products; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§4–5."

$schema: https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema $id: urn:job-application:contracts:owner-separated-write-domains:0.1.0 title: Owner-separated write domains description: >- Review draft for independently writable domains, asynchronous publication, atomic read compositions, named revision-vector seals, and complete immutable archives. Applies the pattern to discovered jobs, application attempts, and Hellscape sessions. A read composition is not a multi-owner write API. x-status: proposed x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt, Parts VI and VIII."

x-contract: name: owner-separated-write-domains version: 0.1.0 maturity: review_draft owner: contracts consumers: [crawler, Circus Tent, Ringmaster, Hellscape, job-hunter, dashboard] conformance_suite: conformance/04-owner-separated-write-domains.md gate: structural_validation_and_OWD_rules scope: - Immutable entity registrations and single-writer domain bindings. - Complete owner revisions and independently acknowledged owner-local writes. - Asynchronous installation of complete revisions into a named read view. - Complete read rows sealed at explicit version vectors. - Fetch-key replacement with complete prior-row archival. - Retention roots protecting archives and their transitive dependencies. non_goals: - A shared database, broker, runtime, or distributed transaction. - A global status replacing independently owned facts. - A new browser abstraction or a change to connector verbs. - A replacement for the kernel lease primitive. - Selection of job-hunter's implementation language or primary store. x-status: proposed x-source: *w
x-compatibility: schema_references: All_$ref_values_are_local common_types: >- Missing, evidence references, artifact references, version pins, clocks, measurements, subject identity, assistance, and attempt context preserve evidence-kernel/0.1.0 wire meanings. attempt_publications: >- AxisRevision and its value types retain application-attempt-lifecycle/0.1.0 field names and record version. They are embedded without assigning a second authoritative revision number. The containing publication receipt and read row belong to this contract. attempt_registration: >- The immutable commission remains an artifact. Registration repeats only the attempt context, execution descriptor, and owner bindings needed here; these must equal the corresponding commissioned values. The registration is not permission to amend the commission. canonicalization: >- Use kernel-jcs-sha256/1: UTF-8 RFC 8785 canonical JSON and SHA-256 digests encoded as sha256:<64 lowercase hexadecimal digits>. Artifact digests identify exact stored bytes. A record never includes its own artifact digest. archive_identity: >- ArchiveRecord.root identifies the exact canonical ArchiveStorageManifest bytes, not the expanded ArchiveRecord or payload_json bytes. The manifest names immutable, locally durable components and deterministically expands into the complete payload_json. This distinction permits bounded metadata archival without reserializing a large downstream domain on crawler writes. x-status: proposed x-source: "contracts/00-evidence-kernel.yaml; contracts/01-application-attempt-lifecycle.yaml; 2-state-bank-crawler-blueprint.json Decision 8."

Neither job owner may overwrite an attempt's execution or application axis. x-status: inferred x-source: "2-state-bank-crawler-blueprint.json §§11.4, 11.14, 11.17; 1-handoff-brief.txt Part VI."

x-validation: x-status: proposed x-source: *w requirements: - >- Validate JSON Schema 2020-12 with format assertions. Reject duplicate YAML keys, non-JSON values, non-finite numbers, unknown versions, and undeclared properties. Decode YAML before hashing; schema anchors are not wire features. - >- Structural validation is necessary but insufficient. All applicable OWD, kernel, and lifecycle authorization, reference, arithmetic, and transition rules must also pass. - >- Only Missing.value may contain serialized null. Every nested absence has one of the six kernel reasons. Empty arrays describe an established empty collection, not an unknown collection. - >- Verify artifact bytes, declared sizes, evidence references, journal prefixes, registration digests, domain identity, and all revision equality constraints. A caller-supplied writer_id or verified flag grants no authority. - >- Mutable rows, URLs, native handles, and current database queries cannot substitute for the immutable components named by a published row or archive.
x-semantic-rules: - id: OWD-OWNER classification: invariant rule: >- Every declared domain has one authenticated logical writer. Entity registration fixes its field set, authority source, writer, storage-domain identity, and publication policy. Temporary workers act through that writer's fenced transition gateway; they do not become additional owners. Each owner_domain is distinct within an entity. consequence: >- A writer may publish only its own complete domain. A changed field outside that domain rejects the entire write. A composed row is never accepted as an update command. Deployment replacement may retain a logical writer identity; ownership transfer requires an explicit versioned migration, not an unjournaled configuration edit. derivation: "Shared field ownership allows one component's refresh to erase another's work." x-status: inferred x-source: *s
- id: OWD-LOCAL-COMMIT classification: invariant rule: >- Commit an owner's authorized effect, revision advance, and journal evidence atomically within that owner's durability boundary. Do not acknowledge before durability. No owner commit acquires a peer-owned write lock or waits for a peer transaction, acknowledgement, or large-payload serialization. consequence: >- A shared contracts workspace, process, or database hostname proves no isolation property. For crawler/downstream writes, independent persistence and I/O admission must be demonstrated. Owner-local journals may be asynchronously imported into a composition journal; a central journal transaction is not required on every owner's write path. derivation: "Two tables behind one serialized storage writer fail Stage1 Decision 8's floor." x-status: extracted x-source: *s
- id: OWD-REVISION classification: invariant rule: >- A domain revision is a complete immutable snapshot, not a patch. revision=previous_revision+1 at the owner. The first revision is 1. The key (entity, domain, revision) identifies exactly one content digest. Identical retries are idempotent; different bytes under that key are an integrity conflict. Stale expected revisions or lease epochs cannot commit. consequence: >- A rejected write changes neither source fields nor publication pointers. Revisions and lease ownership are not application statuses. Claiming a resource does not change its pending operational state. derivation: "Partial writes and unfenced retries create lost updates and duplicate effects." x-status: inferred x-source: "2-state-bank-crawler-blueprint.json §§11.15–11.17; contracts/00-evidence-kernel.yaml."
- id: OWD-PUBLISH classification: invariant rule: >- Owner durability acknowledgement and installation into a read view are different events. Transfer, validate, and durably install all immutable components before atomically advancing the view's domain pointer. The pointer update is bounded metadata work. Publication cannot expose partially transferred bytes. consequence: >- Failed transfer, checksum failure, unavailable peer storage, or publication lag leaves the last complete published revision visible. Reordered delivery cannot roll the current pointer backward. Publication may skip intermediate visible revisions only after verifying their owner revision lineage. An identical installed revision returns its existing receipt. derivation: "Asynchronous publication is safe only when readers see old-or-new, never partial." x-status: extracted x-source: *s
- id: OWD-VIEW classification: invariant rule: >- A LogicalRow contains every declared domain slot and an exact version vector. Each nonzero slot embeds the complete domain document whose artifact digest and installation receipt it names. A zero slot means no publication in this view, or an explicitly inapplicable manual axis. Readers obtain one complete immutable row root. consequence: >- Different owners may be at different publication ages. This is a named, locally available composition, not global cross-owner linearizability. A durable but unpublished downstream update is not silently included. Once a revision has been published, loss of its bytes cannot be disguised as revision zero; report observation_lost and retain the known identity. derivation: "A version vector makes asynchronous freshness visible instead of hiding it behind a whole-row status." x-status: inferred x-source: *s
- id: OWD-SEAL classification: invariant rule: >- A seal names a state and pins all domain revisions selected in a named read view. Its journaled seal-selection event pins the domain document digests and publication receipts before the resulting LogicalRow is registered. The row's input prefix includes that selection event, not its own later artifact-registration event. consequence: >- Seals are immutable and do not freeze future owner writes. observation_closed requires a pinned closed observation publication; it does not establish native termination or final origin absence. A later seal records a new view without changing the earlier cut. derivation: "Without an exact cut, archived rows and diagnostic inputs change when a peer publishes." x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part VI; contracts/01-application-attempt-lifecycle.yaml."
- id: OWD-JOB classification: invariant rule: >- Job acquisition fields belong exclusively to crawler. Product decisions, priorities, materials, and attempt links belong exclusively to downstream. A crawler refresh preserves the separately published downstream domain; it does not copy stale downstream values back into downstream storage. Product evaluations identify the crawler revision they evaluated. consequence: >- A newer crawler revision can make an evaluation stale without deleting it. A content veto is not posting closure. Closure requires authoritative closure evidence, and missing from one crawl is insufficient. An APPLIED display requires a correlated production origin commitment, not a product claim, practice receipt, native completed response, or submit click. derivation: "Crawler semantic candidates and downstream application work have different authorities." x-status: inferred x-source: "2-state-bank-crawler-blueprint.json §§5.6, 11.14, 11.17; 1-handoff-brief.txt Part VI."
- id: OWD-RENDER classification: invariant rule: >- A Pass acquisition must satisfy its declared required content fields. Required content is present, non-null, and correctly typed. A Pass with missing required extraction is rejected as incomplete_extraction, not materialized as a valid job or reclassified as failed rendering. A non-Pass acquisition has pipeline_state=render_failed and reasoned missingness for every content value. consequence: >- Failed render creates no genuine classifier result or successful seen_ids membership. Bypass creates no classifier result. A raw VETO overridden by shadow mode is not a genuine PASS; bypass alone does not shortlist. A later bypass may preserve an earlier genuine applied PASS. derivation: "Render acceptance, relevance classification, and application suitability cannot substitute for one another." x-status: extracted x-source: *c
- id: OWD-FETCH-IDENTITY classification: invariant rule: >- Lookup uses (target, job_id). For A_full, fetch identity is the actual listing source URL. For B, it is canonical URL, uppercase method, actual request-body digest, and representation-determining headers. Exclude ephemeral identity/session headers; do not exclude representation headers to increase cache hits. consequence: >- Preserve query ordering unless endpoint evidence permits normalization. Remove fragments and normalize scheme/host case and default ports. Cookie rotation, run ID, crawl date, response digest, and extractor version are not hidden fetch-key inputs. derivation: "Changing request identity accidentally defeats idempotency and hides the documented freshness limitation." x-status: extracted x-source: "2-state-bank-crawler-blueprint.json §11.16."
- id: OWD-FETCH-NOOP classification: invariant rule: >- An absent root accepts an initial complete crawler domain without a predecessor archive. An existing identical fetch key makes the acquisition write a no-op. No archive is created for that no-op. Independent discovery, lease, classification, and semantic transitions may advance the crawler domain while preserving acquisition and replacement_lineage exactly. consequence: >- A different response under the same key is journaled as new observation, not silently installed as replacement content. Repairing a same-key render_failed acquisition requires an explicitly versioned freshness contract; adding a run nonce is not a repair. derivation: "Stage1 explicitly makes request identity, not response freshness, authoritative for replacement." x-status: extracted x-source: "2-state-bank-crawler-blueprint.json §§11.16 and 15.1."
- id: OWD-REPLACE classification: invariant rule: >- A changed fetch key requires a complete archive of the prior logical row at the named replacement seal. That cut uses the current old crawler revision and the latest fully published downstream revision in the named ingest-side view. An unpublished downstream revision is excluded. The owner-local replacement checks both the old crawler revision/key and the selected local publication pointer before committing. consequence: >- If either checked pointer changed before commit, reject/reselect rather than archiving a mismatched cut. Stage archive components outside the critical section. Commit the new crawler revision, its backward archive link, replacement journal effect, and durable retention protection as one owner-local effect. No updated crawler row may be acknowledged without its complete retrievable archive. A staged orphan is not a committed archive. derivation: "Archive and replacement must not diverge under crashes or concurrent publication." x-status: inferred x-source: *s
- id: OWD-ARCHIVE classification: invariant rule: >- Archive payload_json is the entire previous LogicalRow, including its registration, all domain fields, reasoned nulls, publication receipts, and seal vector. It is not a changed-field diff, crawler-only row, hash list, or lookup of the latest downstream record. consequence: >- Physical immutable extents are permitted only when the archive resolver reconstructs exactly that full typed value without contacting a mutable peer. Complete downstream snapshots are imported before publication. Archive creation reuses their immutable bytes; large downstream JSON must not be serialized under, or awaited by, the crawler writer. derivation: "A locator that later resolves to different or absent fields is not a complete prior-row archive." x-status: extracted x-source: *s
- id: OWD-RETENTION classification: invariant rule: >- A live replacement pins its archive root and every transitive immutable dependency. A retained later archive containing that replacement's backward link also keeps the earlier archive alive. Publishing a newer job revision, deleting a cache entry, or passing a TTL cannot release those dependencies. consequence: >- GC requires journaled proof that no live replacement or retained evidence root reaches the object. Reference checks and deletion are fenced against concurrent pin creation. Release is an explicit retention revision, not mutation of the archived payload. Artifact loss is an integrity incident, not successful GC or permission to silently reconstruct different bytes. derivation: "An immutable archive with reclaimable dependencies is not durable." x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part VI; 2-state-bank-crawler-blueprint.json Decision 8; contracts/00-evidence-kernel.yaml."
- id: OWD-ATTEMPT classification: invariant rule: >- Attempt slots contain the exact lifecycle AxisRevision publications. Their outer slot revision equals the embedded axis revision; the axis, attempt identity, commission digest, owner_domain, and writer_id match registration and commission. The reconciler writes only report. consequence: >- Claim/fact histories remain cumulative and immutable. Late origin commitment can be published while report still uses older input pins. Readers expose that staleness; they neither overwrite the claim nor silently apply the old report to new facts. Manual execution creates no subject publication. derivation: "Owner separation must preserve the cancellation corpus's five orthogonal axes." x-status: extracted x-source: *l
- id: OWD-SESSION classification: invariant rule: >- Hellscape application state is reducer-owned; observation cannot set accepted data, identity verification, or commitment. The diagnostic domain cites exact application and observation input revisions and a journal prefix. It cannot amend either source to fit a finding. consequence: >- A committed fixture application, incomplete telemetry tail, and stale diagnostic can coexist. Confirmation rendering stays observation evidence. The session's pinned attempt-observation copy is verified against its original axis publication, not independently authored lifecycle state. All Hellscape session evidence remains practice and held_in. derivation: "Fixture truth, observed behavior, and judgment have distinct failure modes and authorities." x-status: inferred x-source: "3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§3–4 and 10; 1-handoff-brief.txt Part III."
- id: OWD-TIME-PROVENANCE classification: invariant rule: >- Every measurement retains clock_id, boot_id, origin, censoring, and an exact, bounded, or unavailable estimate. No cross-clock or cross-restart subtraction is permitted. Publication delay cannot be computed by subtracting arbitrary source and destination UTC annotations. Provenance and writer authorization are assigned and checked at ingestion. consequence: >- Zero is a valid exact duration, never missingness. Unknown publication lag stays unavailable or bounded. Imported origin facts retain their original authority and correlation evidence; import does not turn a manual observation into a server-origin fact. derivation: "The timing defect and claim-as-fact counterexamples remain applicable at the storage boundary." x-status: extracted x-source: *k
x-proposed-mechanisms: - id: OWD-EXTENT-ENCODING decision: >- Use owner-domain-extents/1 for archive manifests. Each published domain already has a complete immutable document artifact. An archive manifest pins those document artifacts, the entity registration artifact, and the full seal. Expansion inserts the verified documents into the LogicalRow shape defined here. rationale: >- The metadata size depends on the fixed number of domains, not downstream payload size. This reconciles complete logical archives with the explicit prohibition on downstream serialization in the crawler critical path. flip_condition: >- A different representation may replace this encoding in a new version only if it demonstrates exact full-row reconstruction, content addressing, transitive retention, and equivalent non-blocking write behavior. x-status: proposed x-source: *s
- id: OWD-READ-ROOT decision: >- Install immutable LogicalRow roots atomically in each read view. A composition service owns only that derived pointer and its publication journal; it gains no source-domain write authority. rationale: >- An atomic root prevents readers from assembling half a publication while permitting each source owner to acknowledge writes independently. flip_condition: >- A storage-native snapshot mechanism is acceptable if it returns the same explicit domain pins and passes old-or-new, delayed-publication, crash, and archive-race tests without a cross-owner transaction. x-status: proposed x-source: *w
x-fetch-key-profile: id: crawler-fetch-key/1 formulas: B: "SHA-256(JCS([target, 'B', job_id, canonical_request]))" A_full: "SHA-256(JCS([target, 'A_full', job_id, listing_source_url]))" canonical_request_fields: [url, method, body_hash, header_identity_set] framing: >- Arrays are length-unambiguous JSON arrays. header_identity_set is ordered by normalized header name with deterministic value ordering declared by the endpoint. Preserve meaningful multi-value and query order. x-status: proposed x-source: "2-state-bank-crawler-blueprint.json §11.16 specifies inputs; framing is a Step 0 wire proposal."
x-archive-expansion: algorithm: - Verify root.digest and size against canonical storage_manifest bytes. - Load and verify the registration artifact; retain its digest. - For each nonzero domain pin, load its complete document and verify its digest and owner binding. - Preserve every zero-domain Missing envelope exactly. - >- Construct LogicalRow with record_type=logical_row, this contract version, the manifest entity, the complete registration, registration_digest, each expanded domain slot, and the manifest seal_point. - >- Require structural and semantic equality with ArchiveRecord.payload_json. No current owner lookup, default insertion, redaction, or revision upgrade is part of expansion. - Verify local durability and retention of every transitive dependency before replacement acknowledgement. x-status: proposed x-source: *w
x-open-evidence: - missing: Deployment proof of independently reserved ingest, downstream, and snapshot-transfer I/O. resolution: >- Run the two-writer and archive-load suite on the chosen storage deployment. Stage1 A2 and A7 are assumptions and workload baselines, not portfolio-wide guarantees. No source benchmark certifies a chosen new deployment. x-status: uncertain x-source: "2-state-bank-crawler-blueprint.json A2, A7, Decision 8."
- missing: Precise types and semantics of several legacy Firestore fields, including closingDate and priorityHint. resolution: >- Preserve observed closing-date text without inventing a timezone or deadline. Treat the numeric priority representation here as a proposed product-owned hint, not an extracted scoring rubric. Reconcile actual producers against fixtures before migration; preserve originals in registered source artifacts. x-status: uncertain x-source: "6-get-a-job.xml.txt docs/contracts/firestore-collections.md supplies field names, not executable schemas."

The atomic commit event records these identities without a cyclic reference to this receipt's later artifact digest. x-status: proposed x-source: *w

RetentionPinRevision: type: object additionalProperties: false required: - record_type - schema_version - pin_id - owner_domain - writer_id - revision - previous_revision - dependent - archive_root - state - release_ref - evidence_prefix - evidence_refs properties: record_type: {const: archive_retention_pin, x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} schema_version: {$ref: "#/$defs/SchemaVersion", x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} pin_id: {$ref: "#/$defs/Identifier", x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} owner_domain: {$ref: "#/$defs/Identifier", x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} writer_id: {$ref: "#/$defs/Identifier", x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} revision: {$ref: "#/$defs/PositiveInteger", x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} previous_revision: {$ref: "#/$defs/Revision", x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} dependent: {$ref: "#/$defs/RetentionDependent", x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} archive_root: {$ref: "#/$defs/ArtifactReference", x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} state: {enum: [active, released], x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} release_ref: {$ref: "#/$defs/MaybeEvidenceRef", x-status: proposed, x-source: *w} evidence_prefix: {$ref: "#/$defs/JournalPrefix", x-status: inferred, x-source: *k} evidence_refs: {$ref: "#/$defs/SupportRefs", x-status: inferred, x-source: *k} allOf: - if: {properties: {state: {const: active}}} then: {properties: {release_ref: {$ref: "#/$defs/Inapplicable"}}} else: {properties: {release_ref: {$ref: "#/$defs/EvidenceRef"}}} description: >- Written only by the registered retention authority for the archive's persistence domain. Initial revision is active. dependent and archive_root never change under a pin ID. Release requires evidenced retirement of that root and preserves other roots' protection. GC may reclaim bytes only after all direct and transitive protections are absent under a concurrency-safe check. Released pins and retention history remain journaled; they do not mutate archived content. x-status: proposed x-source: *w

$schema: https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema $id: urn:job-application:contracts:suggested-fix-registry:0.1.0 title: Suggested-fix registry description: >- Review draft for evidence-backed, scoped recommendations that turn recorded application and laboratory findings into actionable improvements.
