RegistrySnapshot supplies the artifact pinned by FixReference.registry. registry_pin: >- VersionPin.id equals RegistrySnapshot.registry_id; VersionPin.version equals registry_version; artifact_digest hashes the complete canonical snapshot. The snapshot contains no digest of itself. instance_lookup: >- A snapshot contains at most one revision of each rule_instance_id. Therefore the kernel reference resolves one exact immutable instance without adding an instance_revision field to the kernel wire shape. plan_lookup: >- FixReference.verification_plan must identify the same complete plan artifact as the selected RuleInstance.verification_plan. measurements: >- This contract stores no measured durations or measured numeric outcomes. Verification cites journaled kernel Measurements, diagnostics, and native evidence. Integer counts here declare required evidence or record revisions; they are not measured performance claims. canonicalization: >- Use kernel-jcs-sha256/1: UTF-8 RFC 8785 canonical JSON and SHA-256 encoded as sha256:<64 lowercase hexadecimal digits>. Artifact digests identify exact stored bytes. Redacted exports have new identities. x-status: proposed x-source: *k
x-ownership: rule_classes: writer: registry_curator authority: >- Defines a proposed intervention family, its evidence requirements, contraindications, and verification obligations. Model-authored material remains a recorded proposal until adopted by this authenticated writer. class_reviews: writer: authenticated_human_reviewer authority: >- Approves, rejects, or revokes one exact class version. The operator may occupy this role; a second human or separate service is not required. A model, connector, or subject cannot self-issue human approval. rule_instances: writer: registry_curator authority: >- Records a concrete proposal and its evidence assessments. It cannot rewrite the cited diagnostic, subject claim, origin fact, or capability. catalog: writer: registry_publisher authority: >- Publishes a complete immutable selection of class, review, and instance revisions. Publication is an owner-local effect, not a transaction over diagnostic or execution owners. recommendations: writer: consumer_assessor authority: >- Hellscape or another authorized diagnostic consumer decides whether a rule instance matches its evidence. A connector declares observations and capabilities; it does not assess its own qualification. verification: writer: verification_assessor authority: >- Assesses a pinned plan against independent retained evidence. Native product test output may be evidence, but is not self-certifying judgment. implementation: writer: target_product_owner authority: >- Changes source, configuration, or operating procedures under that product's authorization. No registry record performs this write. x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Parts VI and IX; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§3.2, 4.7, and 6.6."
x-source-reconciliation: - decision: >- The handoff fixes the registry schema at Step 0 and defers implementation to M3. Hellscape's M3 registry milestone therefore supplies later matching, counterfactual, minimization, and verification implementation, not a reason to postpone the reference format. x-status: extracted x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Parts VII–VIII; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §7."
- decision: >- Human approval attaches to an exact rule class version, as specified by the handoff's outer loop. Instances still require their own diagnostic support, scope match, contraindication checks, and verification plan. Class approval is neither instance verification nor execution authority. x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part IX; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §6.6."
- decision: >- Native learn-run-heal cache changes remain execution-layer behavior. An immediate selector-cache update described by Circus Tent is not automatically a reviewed fix-registry instance or proof of improvement. Conversely, this registry does not impose human approval on every already-authorized native healing action. x-status: inferred x-source: "4-circus-tent-arch.md §5.6; 1-handoff-brief.txt Parts V and IX."
- decision: >- Historical cancellation, timing, and isolation descriptions may inform rule proposals, but do not certify a current subject revision. In particular, the invalid isolation write control cannot support a confirmed non-isolation diagnosis or a remedy premised on that diagnosis. x-status: extracted x-source: *e
- decision: >- A fix may target the subject, connector, planner, fixture, environment, or policy according to supported attribution. An adapter overclaim or a fixture defect must not be relabeled as a subject defect to fit a rule. x-status: extracted x-source: *d
- decision: >- The registry does not contain a universal patch representation or a cross-browser primitive API. A class may describe a common problem, but Circus Tent and Ringmaster receive separate product-specific instances and verification evidence. x-status: inferred x-source: *b
- decision: >- No handoff amendment is introduced. Review, catalog, and verification record shapes below are proposed mechanisms for its existing commitments. x-status: proposed x-source: *w
x-validation: requirements: - >- Decode YAML into JSON-compatible values. Reject duplicate keys, non-finite numbers, undeclared fields, unknown record versions, and unresolved local schema references. Enforce JSON Schema 2020-12. - >- Structural validity is necessary but insufficient. Enforce all applicable FIX rules, evidence-kernel rules, and lifecycle scope/authority rules. Caller-supplied writer IDs, evidence labels, or review decisions do not authenticate themselves. - >- Only Missing.value may contain serialized null. Required fields cannot disappear to evade missingness. Empty arrays mean an established empty collection, not unknown contents. - >- Resolve and hash-check every artifact and evidence reference. Verify copied diagnostic IDs, analysis revisions, input prefixes, finding IDs, subject identities, and capability scopes against their actual records. - >- Text predicates are reviewed declarative requirements, not executable expressions. Procedures and oracles are immutable referenced artifacts. This schema does not authorize loading code from a rule or executing a model-generated command. x-status: proposed x-source: *w
x-semantic-rules: - id: FIX-JOURNAL classification: invariant rule: >- Every citable class, review, instance, plan, catalog, and verification receipt is immutable and registered in the journal. Its evidence_prefix contains its support and locally journaled imports, not its own later artifact-registration event. Retain original source scope and provenance through imports. consequence: >- A finding citation resolves a published diagnostic and a finding within that diagnostic's pinned input prefix. Unjournaled notes, mutable source files, current web pages, or a plausible model explanation are not evidence. derivation: "Anything not journaled cannot be cited, and retroactive evidence destroys replay." x-status: extracted x-source: *h
- id: FIX-VERSIONS classification: invariant rule: >- Record identities and revisions are immutable. Reusing an identity/version or identity/revision with different bytes is an integrity conflict. Revision chains start at 1 and advance by one. Supersession preserves previous bytes and resolves to the immediately preceding compatible record. consequence: >- A changed class definition requires a new class version and fresh human review. A new target revision, subject version, configured mode, interface, or applicability cell requires a new instance identity and its own evidence assessment. Prior verification cannot be inherited. derivation: "A prior-version finding must not become a current-version assumption." x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part VI; contracts/00-evidence-kernel.yaml EK-CAPABILITY."
- id: FIX-CLASS-REVIEW classification: invariant rule: >- An eligible recommendation resolves to an approved review of the exact class artifact in its pinned registry snapshot. Verify the reviewer as an authenticated human under the pinned review policy. First reviews may approve or reject; revocation names a prior approved review chain. consequence: >- Model proposals, approvals of a different class version, and instance-only approvals do not satisfy this rule. A later rejection or revocation changes future catalog eligibility without editing historical diagnostics. Deliberately selecting an older catalog to evade a visible revocation is prohibited. derivation: "The reviewed outer loop approves rule classes; the judged component cannot approve itself." x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part IX; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §6.6."
- id: FIX-CATALOG classification: invariant rule: >- A registry snapshot pins complete class, current review, and instance artifacts at a named prefix. Publish it only after all referenced bytes are durable and validated. Readers see one complete old or new snapshot, never partial entries. consequence: >- A catalog may contain pending or rejected proposals for inspection; their presence is not recommendation eligibility. A new diagnostic uses the catalog head evidenced at its selection boundary. Exact re-derivation uses the recorded snapshot, not today's head or review state. derivation: "Asynchronous publication and deterministic diagnostic replay require immutable input cuts." x-status: inferred x-source: "2-state-bank-crawler-blueprint.json Decision 8; contracts/00-evidence-kernel.yaml EK-DIAGNOSTIC."
- id: FIX-SCOPE classification: invariant rule: >- An instance targets one product and one evidenced component version key. Every applicability cell pins task, environment, execution mode, subject identity when present, assistance, state policies, and attempt scope. A recommendation must name and match an existing cell; matching a symptom string alone is insufficient. consequence: >- A shared rule class does not share native implementation. A Circus Tent instance cannot supply a Ringmaster repair or vice versa. Native-binding remedies refer to the particular product's native surface without introducing a shared ElementHandle or primitive signature. derivation: "Cross-browser internal unification repeats the Stagehand-on-Juggler failure." x-status: inferred x-source: *b
- id: FIX-REQUIRED-EVIDENCE classification: invariant rule: >- Instances reproduce every class evidence requirement unchanged and may add requirements. For each requirement and applicability cell, record exactly one EvidenceCheck. met requires the declared predicate, minimum distinct evidence units, allowed source scopes, and exact target/version support. Unsupported or missing observations remain indeterminate. consequence: >- Count independently identified attempts, artifacts, or fixture configurations, not duplicate callbacks, duplicate imports, or multiple findings from the same unit. Evidence labels are checked against ingestion, not trusted because a proposal supplies them. derivation: "Repeated delivery and documentary claims must not manufacture experimental support." x-status: inferred x-source: "3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§4.3–4.7 and 6.6; contracts/00-evidence-kernel.yaml."
- id: FIX-ATTRIBUTION classification: invariant rule: >- Keep symptom, causal hypothesis, defect locus, and proposed intervention distinct. A concrete remedy requires confirmed or supported attribution at the scope it claims. Native absence, an observed violation, and an indeterminate result cannot substitute for one another. consequence: >- Unknown causes may be retained as suspected proposals for investigation, but do not produce an eligible suggested_fix. Invalid controls, unexposed work, missing dependencies, or an unmapped connector operation cannot establish the corresponding subject defect. Preserve contrary evidence. derivation: "Naming an internal selector or isolation defect without valid controls is unsupported attribution." x-status: extracted x-source: "3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§1.3, 4.1, 4.3–4.7; 5-browser-qualification.md."
- id: FIX-CONTRAINDICATIONS classification: invariant rule: >- Instances reproduce every class contraindication unchanged and may add contraindications. Record exactly one check per contraindication and applicability cell. An eligible recommendation requires evidenced absence of each applicable contraindication. consequence: >- present and unknown both withhold the suggestion. Silence is not absence. A human class approval cannot waive missing controls, incompatible native surfaces, conflicting facts, or a contraindication named by the class. derivation: "Evidence-backed recommendations must state where their reasoning or intervention is unsafe." x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part VIII; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §6.6."
- id: FIX-RECOMMEND classification: invariant rule: >- Emit FixReference only when the exact class is approved, the target and cell match, required evidence checks are met, contraindications are absent, attribution is supported, and a complete falsifiable plan is registered. The consumer independently verifies these conditions rather than trusting a proposal's confidence label. consequence: >- No completed verification receipt is required to recommend an unimplemented change. Without an eligible rule, emit Missing with a kernel reason and useful detail. M1 may use not_enabled; insufficient evidence uses not_observed or observation_lost, not a new null-reason vocabulary. derivation: "A suggestion must be justified, but requiring a repair to be verified before suggesting it is circular." x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part VII; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§4.4, 4.7, and 6.6."
- id: FIX-PRACTICE classification: invariant rule: >- Preserve practice/production and held_in/held_out in every application scope. Hellscape is practice and held_in; employer origins are held_out. Diagnostic and verification references retain their original attempt kinds. Historical and synthetic evidence remain explicitly labeled. consequence: >- A laboratory result can motivate an execution-layer improvement but cannot establish production commitment, origin representativeness, or held-out transfer. A production recommendation needs its declared production-scope support; a practice-only check remains practice-only. derivation: "Tuning against Hellscape is not qualification for a real employer's forms." x-status: extracted x-source: *b
- id: FIX-PLAN classification: invariant rule: >- The plan names the baseline target, exact applicability cells, verification methods, immutable procedures and oracles, pass/fail predicates, evidence requirements, declared budgets, and stop conditions. It includes every class-required verification role and identifies controlled differences for comparisons. consequence: >- Candidate evaluation and regression checks are required by this proposed schema. A plan claiming improvement must include a defensible baseline; a plan claiming transfer must include that transfer scope. An absent or unresolved procedure cannot be replaced by "rerun until it works." derivation: "A recommendation without a falsifiable verification path is not actionable learning." x-status: inferred x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part VIII; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§6.6 and 7.2."
- id: FIX-VERIFY classification: invariant rule: >- Verification receipts identify the exact instance and plan, actual target revision, realized scopes, assessor, and evidence for every planned check. Preserve invalid controls, incomparability, skipped checks, and contrary results. A newly tested subject version requires its own capability descriptors and observations. consequence: >- criterion_met describes a plan oracle, not application success or native capability presence. Underlying diagnostic assessments retain capability, opportunity, and result separately. Missing required checks prevent a claim that the plan was satisfied. No portfolio-wide qualified flag exists. derivation: "A skipped required step is not a pass, and verification cannot inherit a predecessor's capability." x-status: inferred x-source: "5-browser-qualification.md; 1-handoff-brief.txt Part VI; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §6.6."
- id: FIX-NO-AUTO-PATCH classification: invariant rule: >- Class approval, recommendation, implementation, and verification are separate facts with separate authorities. No record here invokes a browser, patches a product, changes an active task, promotes a subject version, or commissions an application. consequence: >- The autonomous fixture-variant loop does not gain authority to activate execution-layer fixes. Implementation follows the product owner's change process. Production work still requires its own commission and permissions. derivation: "Hellscape diagnoses the framework; it does not silently repair the subject or become the job pipeline." x-status: extracted x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Parts III and IX; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§1.2 and 3.2."
- id: FIX-SAFE-VERIFICATION classification: invariant rule: >- Offline fixture replay and diagnostic re-derivation invoke no subject, browser, or external mutation. They cannot by themselves demonstrate changed native execution behavior. Browser or origin observations are separately authorized new attempts, not exact replay. consequence: >- A plan cannot resolve uncertain delivery by resubmitting with a fresh key, switching executors, or forcing a second production application as an A/B control. Preserve lifecycle duplicate-risk review and same-kind lineage. A plan's mutation_policy is a restriction, never an authorization grant. derivation: "External commitment cannot be rolled back by local replay or observer termination." x-status: inferred x-source: "contracts/01-application-attempt-lifecycle.yaml LIFE-IDEMPOTENCY; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§6.5 and 10.8."
- id: FIX-TIME-NULL classification: invariant rule: >- Measurements cited by evidence or verification retain the kernel's origin, clock_id, boot_id, exact/bounded/unavailable estimate, and censoring. Compare matching semantic intervals or defensible bounds; never subtract across clocks or boots, and never use UTC annotations as elapsed time. consequence: >- A subject-reported exact zero remains zero, not missing and not independent proof of fast execution. Missing native timing remains unavailable. manual_override missingness requires an authenticated journaled decision and cannot erase an original claim or fact. derivation: "The _elapsed() defect and ambiguous nulls are paid-for integration failures." x-status: extracted x-source: *k
- id: FIX-RETENTION classification: invariant rule: >- Retained recommendations pin their registry, instance, class review, plan, diagnostic, and evidence dependencies transitively. Supersession or revocation does not permit deleting bytes needed by historical reports. Restrict artifacts containing candidate data, native bodies, or credentials. consequence: >- A public rule description contains no secret or unnecessary personal data. Artifact loss produces an integrity incident and honest missing evidence, never reconstruction of different bytes under the old digest. derivation: "A reproducible learning event requires durable evidence, not mutable links." x-status: inferred x-source: "contracts/00-evidence-kernel.yaml EK-ARTIFACTS; 6-get-a-job.xml.txt AGENTS.md."
x-reference-order: sequence: - Publish the source diagnostic with its original finding and reasoned null or earlier recommendation. - Register the class definition, its human review, and the change proposal artifacts. - Register the verification plan, naming the planned rule_instance_id but not the future instance digest. - Register the rule instance citing the already published diagnostic and plan. - Publish the immutable registry snapshot containing that instance. - A later diagnostic revision may cite the snapshot and instance through FixReference. - Later verification receipts cite the exact instance digest and newly collected evidence. constraints: - Never edit the source diagnostic to attach its newly created recommendation. - An instance cannot use the diagnostic that first introduces that same instance as its own causal support. - A plan does not contain the digest of the instance that contains the plan reference. - A verification receipt does not retroactively become evidence available when the proposal was made. x-status: proposed x-source: "contracts/00-evidence-kernel.yaml EK-DIAGNOSTIC; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§4.7 and 10.7."
x-provisionals: - decision: Exact applicability cells rather than an executable wildcard-matching language. rationale: >- Step 0 can validate scope and evidence without inventing a rule engine. Manual assessment and later deterministic matchers can consume the same records. Broad rule classes remain reusable; instances remain accountable. flip_condition: >- Add a versioned predicate language only when recurring reviewed instances demonstrate necessary matching semantics that finite cells cannot express economically, with equivalent evidence and scope conformance. x-status: proposed x-source: *w
- decision: Verification receipts have per-check results and no aggregate repair-success status. rationale: >- This keeps regression, comparability, transfer, and missing checks visible. A read-side summary may be derived from the complete pinned plan and receipt. flip_condition: >- Add a derived summary in a new version only if consumers repeatedly implement inconsistent reductions and a common reduction preserves all scope, validity, and missing-evidence distinctions. x-status: proposed x-source: *w

An empty catalog is valid. x-status: uncertain x-source: "1-handoff-brief.txt Part VII; 3-hellscape-blueprint.md §§4.7 and 6.6."

Candidate checks cannot be criterion_met without an identified candidate, implementation evidence appropriate to the change, and the candidate's own observed results. Baseline checks use the pinned baseline identity. Comparative conclusions require valid controlled comparisons; source inspection and offline replay alone cannot prove new native behavior.
